模块 ara::exec — Execution Management

用户指南 AI 生成 / AI generated

自动生成的描述、内容源自引用的AUTOSAR-R25-11文档（SWS规范和随附的标准文档）——不是正式的AUTOSAR文本。标记为解释的陈述是从来源得出的结论。

Rolle & Verwendungszweck

Das Modul ara::exec (Execution Management) ist die zentrale Instanz für die Prozesssteuerung, das Scheduling und das Zustandsmanagement auf der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Es bildet das Bindeglied zwischen dem zugrundeliegenden POSIX-Betriebssystem und der modularen AUTOSAR-Laufzeitumgebung [SWS_EM_01001].

Die Kernaufgaben von ara::exec umfassen:

  • Prozesslebenszyklus-Steuerung: Deterministischer Start, Überwachung und geordnete Terminierung modellierter POSIX-Prozesse basierend auf Execution- und Machine-Manifesten.
  • Zustandsverwaltung über Funktionsgruppen: Abbildung von Systemzuständen auf FunctionGroups (z. B. MachineState oder anwendungsspezifische Gruppen), deren Zustände (FunctionGroupStates) exakt festlegen, welche Prozesse aktiv sein müssen.
  • Lebenszyklus-Handshake (ExecutionClient): Jeder gestartete Prozess muss seine erfolgreiche Initialisierung aktiv über den ExecutionClient an das Execution Management melden.
  • Ressourcen- und Scheduling-Konfiguration: Zuweisung von Betriebssystem-Ressourcen (CPU-Affinität, Speichergrenzen via ResourceGroups) sowie Scheduling-Strategien (z. B. Echtzeit-Scheduling via SCHED_FIFO / SCHED_RR).
  • Fehlererkennung und -wiederherstellung: Erkennung von Prozessabstürzen, Timeout-Verletzungen beim Hochfahren und Signalisierung von Fehlern an das State Management.

Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge

Die Schnittstellenarchitektur von ara::exec unterscheidet streng zwischen der Schnittstelle für reguläre Anwendungsprozesse (ExecutionClient) und den Steuer-Schnittstellen für privilegierte Plattform-Komponenten (StateClient):

  • ExecutionClient: Normale Adaptive Applications instanziieren den ara::exec::ExecutionClient [SWS_EM_02002]. Sobald die anwendungseigene Initialisierung abgeschlossen ist und die Anwendung bereit für den Normalbetrieb ist, ruft sie ReportExecutionState(ExecutionState::kRunning) auf [SWS_EM_02003]. Vor der regulären Beendigung nach Erhalt eines Terminierungssignals signalisiert sie analog ReportExecutionState(ExecutionState::kTerminating).
  • FunctionGroup und FunctionGroupState: Eine Funktionsgruppe bündelt eine Menge von Prozessen, die gemeinsam aktiviert oder deaktiviert werden [SWS_EM_02272]. Jeder gültige Zustand wird durch ein FunctionGroupState-Objekt repräsentiert [SWS_EM_02273]. Standardmäßig besitzt jede Funktionsgruppe die Zustände Off, Verify und Terminate.
  • Zustandswechsel-Schnittstelle: Privilegierte Management-Applikationen (State Management) fordern Zustandsänderungen über SetState() an [SWS_EM_02285]. Dieser Aufruf liefert ein ara::core::Future zurück, das erst erfüllt wird, wenn alle für den Zielzustand erforderlichen Prozesse erfolgreich gestartet wurden bzw. abgelöste Prozesse terminiert sind.
  • Betriebssystem-Interaktion: Execution Management startet Prozesse typischerweise als Kindprozesse via fork() / execve() und richtet Signal-Handler ein, um den Exit-Status über waitpid() zu überwachen.

Interaktionsfluss

Der Interaktionsfluss verknüpft State Management, Execution Management und die einzelnen Anwendungsprozesse. Fordert das State Management einen Zustandswechsel an, berechnet das EM die Prozess-Differenzmenge, startet neue Prozesse und wartet auf deren kRunning-Rückmeldung. Beim Herunterfahren wird den Prozessen ein SIGTERM zugestellt, woraufhin diese geordnet terminieren.

Interaktionsdiagramm: Koordination von Function-Group-Zustandswechseln zwischen State Management und Execution Management sowie Prozesslebenszyklus-Meldungen über den ExecutionClient. Quellen: [SWS_EM_02002], [SWS_EM_02003], [SWS_EM_02272] und [SWS_EM_02285].

Konfiguration & Fehlerbehandlung

Fehlerhafte Prozesszustände und Übergangsfehler werden über die ExecErrorDomain bzw. den Fehlercode-Enum ExecErrc signalisiert [SWS_EM_02286]. Die wesentlichen Überwachungs- und Fehlerpfade umfassen:

  • Startup- und Termination-Timeouts: Meldet ein gestarteter Prozess innerhalb des im Manifest konfigurierten Zeitfensters nicht kRunning, wertet das EM dies als Startfehler. Reagiert ein Prozess beim Herunterfahren nicht rechtzeitig auf SIGTERM, erzwingt das EM die Beendigung nach Ablauf des Termination-Timeouts mittels SIGKILL.
  • Unerwartete Prozessterminierung: Stirbt ein Prozess unerwartet während des Normalbetriebs, wechselt die zugehörige Funktionsgruppe in den Zustand Undefined. Das EM benachrichtigt das State Management über den undefinedStateCallback [SWS_EM_02553], welches über vordefinierte Recovery-Strategien (z. B. Prozessneustart oder Steuergeräte-Reset) entscheidet.
  • Fehlercodes: Fehlgeschlagene Zustandswechsel werden im Future über ExecErrc::kFailed, ExecErrc::kCancelled oder ExecErrc::kGeneralError ausgewiesen [SWS_EM_02287].

FOLGENDE RICHTLINIEN SIND STRIKT BINDEND:
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P12_15",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nThis document is the software specification of the\nExecution Management\nfunc-\ntional cluster within the\nAdaptive Platform Foundation\n.\nExecution Management\nis responsible for the management of all aspects of sys-\ntem execution including platform initialization and the startup / shutdown of\nAppli-\ncations\n.\nExecution Management\nworks with, and configures, the\nOperating\nSystem\nto perform run-time scheduling of\nApplications\n.\nChapter 7 describes how\nExecution Management\nconcepts are realized within the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n.\n1.1 What is Execution Management?\nExecution Management\nis the functional cluster within the\nAdaptive Platform\nFoundation\nthat is responsible for platform initialization and the startup and shutdown\nof\nModelled Processes\n.\nModelled Processes\nare self-contained, e.g. have in-\nternal control of thread creation.\nExecution Management\nperforms these tasks us-\ning information contained within one or more\nManifest\ncontent such as when and\nhow\nExecutables\nshould be started.\nExecution Management\nalso provides sup-\nport for State Management (see Section 7.5), Deterministic Execution (see Section\n7.6), and Security (Section 7.9).\nThe\nExecution Management\nfunctional cluster is part of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive\nPlatform\n. However, the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nis usually not exclusively\nused within a single AUTOSAR System as the vehicle is also equipped with a number\nof ECUs developed on the\nAUTOSAR Classic Platform\n. The System design for the\nentire vehicle will therefore cover both\nAUTOSAR Classic Platform\nECUs as well as\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Machines\n.\n1.2 Interaction with AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive\nThe set of programming interfaces to the\nAdaptive Applications\nis called\nAUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive (ARA). The interfaces that constitute ARA include\nthose of\nExecution Management\nspecified in Chapter 8.\nExecution Management\n, in common with other\nApplications\nis assumed to be a\nprocess executed on a POSIX compliant operating system.\nExecution Management\nis responsible for initiating execution of the processes in all the Functional Clusters,\nAdaptive AUTOSAR Services, and user-level\nApplications\n. Therefore, Execution\nManagement has no standardized dependencies. The launching order of\nApplica-\ntions\nis derived by\nExecution Management\naccording to the specification defined\nin this document to ensure proper startup of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n.\n12 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P13_16",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 13,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe Adaptive AUTOSAR Services are provided via mechanisms provided by the\nCommunication Management\nfunctional cluster [1] of the\nAdaptive Platform\nFoundation\n. In order to use the Adaptive AUTOSAR Services, the functional clusters\nin the\nAdaptive Platform Foundation\nmust be properly initialized beforehand.\nPlease refer to the respective specifications regarding more information on\nCommuni-\ncation Management\n.\n13 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P14_17",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 14,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n2 Acronyms and abbreviations\nAll technical terms used throughout this document  except the ones listed here  can\nbe found in the official [2] AUTOSAR Glossary or [3] TPS Manifest Specification."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P14_18",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 14,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "A type of\nModelled Process\nwith an associated\nExecutable\nwhere\nreportingBehavior\nis set to\ndoesNotReportExecu-\ntionState\n([TPS_MANI_01279]). Please note that the\nNon-\nreporting Process\nwas\nnot\ndeveloped for the\nAUTOSAR Adap-\ntive Platform\nand for this reason it is not using\nAdaptive\nPlatform Services\n. For example, it is not using\nara::\nexec::ExecutionClient\nAPI and therefore cannot report\nEx-\necution State\nto\nExecution Management\n. In general, this\ntype of a process is intended to allow integration of a software\nthat cannot be modified for use with the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive\nPlatform\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P14_19",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 14,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "A type of\nModelled Process\nthat has\nterminationBehav-\nior\nconfigured to\nprocessIsSelfTerminating\n. This type of\nModelled Process\nis allowed to self initiate termination proce-\ndure (i.e. just terminate with exit status\nEXIT_SUCCESS\n), or wait\nfor\nExecution Management\nto initiate termination procedure\nvia\nSIGTERM\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P15_20",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P15_21",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The event consumed by\nExecution Management\nwhen a\nModelled Process\nterminates without justified reason, for ex-\nample:\n•\ntermination without prior request where\ntermination-\nBehavior\nis configured to\nprocessIsNotSelfTermi-\nnating\n.\n•\ntermination before reporting\nkRunning\n.\nPlease note that every\nUnexpected Self-termination\nis\nalso an\nUnexpected Termination\n, so requirements for the\nlater apply here as well."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P15_22",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The event consumed by\nExecution Management\nwhen a\nModelled Process\nterminates with exit status other than 0\n(\nEXIT_SUCCESS\n). Any kind of unhandled signal will result in an\nUnexpected Termination\nand thus a non 0 exit status."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {

      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "State Management\ninterface to\nExecution Management\nto\nsupport\nFunction Group State\nand\nMachine State\nman-\nagement."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P16_25",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "A state entered by\nExecution Management\nin response to a\nsituation that it cannot resolve. In the state,\nExecution Man-\nagement\nstops taking any further actions, terminates all pro-\ncesses managed by\nExecution Management\nand provides a\nfacility for further project-specific handling."
    },

      "source_page": 17,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe following technical terms used throughout this document are defined in the official\n[2] AUTOSAR Glossary or [3] TPS Manifest Specification  they are repeated here for\ntracing purposes."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P18_27",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 18,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n3 Related documentation\n3.1 Input documents & related standards and norms\nThe main documents that serve as input for the specification of the\nExecution Man-\nagement\nare:\n[1] Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement\n[2] Glossary\nAUTOSAR_FO_TR_Glossary\n[3] Specification of Manifest\nAUTOSAR_AP_TPS_ManifestSpecification\n[4] Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core\n[5] Requirements on Execution Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_RS_ExecutionManagement\n[6] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Software Architecture\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture\n[7] Methodology for Adaptive Platform\nAUTOSAR_AP_TR_Methodology\n[8] Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement\n[9] Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement\n[10] Guidelines for using Adaptive Platform interfaces\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines\n[11] Safety Requirements for AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform and AUTOSAR Classic\nPlatform\nAUTOSAR_FO_RS_Safety\n[12] Standard for Information TechnologyPortable Operating System Interface\n(POSIX(R)) Base Specifications, Issue 7\nhttp://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/\n[13] Algirdas Avizienis, Jean-Claude Laprie, Brian Randell, and Carl Landwehr, 'Basic\nConcepts and Taxonomy of Dependable and Secure Computing', IEEE Transac-\ntions on Dependable and Secure Computing, Vol. 1, No. 1, January-March 2004\n[14] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Design\n18 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },

      "source_element": null,

      "source_page": 19,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign\n[15] Explanation of Identity and Access Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_IdentityAndAccessManagement\n3.2 Further applicable specification\nAUTOSAR provides a core specification [4] which is also applicable for\nExecution\nManagement\n. The chapter General requirements for all FunctionalClusters of this\nspecification shall be considered as an additional and required specification for imple-\nmentation of\nExecution Management\n.\n19 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P20_29",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 20,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Known Limitations\nThis chapter lists known limitations of\nExecution Management\nand their relation to\nthis release of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nwith the intent to provide an indi-\ncation how\nExecution Management\nwithin the context of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive\nPlatform\nwill evolve in future releases.\nThe following functionality is mentioned within this document but is not fully specified\nin this release:\nSection 7.7 Resource Limitation and Section 7.8 Fault Tolerance\n these sec-\ntions have been expanded in this release but are not complete. In particular\nthe contents will be expanded with more properties and formal requirements in\nthe next release.\nSection 7.6.4 describes synchronization requirements for redundant deterministic ex-\necution that were required but not elaborated in 7.6.2. The interface of using com-\nmunication APIs other than\nara::com\nis not in the scope of the specification. We\nfocus on the single domain synchronization for the current release, i.e. the redundant\ndeterministic execution is in the same OS or ECU. The models and configuration for\ndeterministic synchronization and the details of interaction with Software Lockstep will\nbe specified in a later release.\nSection 6.1 details requirements from\nExecution Management\nRequirement Spec-\nification [5] that are not elaborated within this specification. The presence of these\nrequirements in this document ensures that the requirement tracing is complete and\nalso provides an indication of how\nExecution Management\nwill evolve in future re-\nleases of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n.\nThe functionality described above is subject to modification and will be considered for\ninclusion in a future release of this document.\n20 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P21_30",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 21,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5 Dependencies to other Functional Clusters\nThis chapter provides an overview of the dependencies to other Functional Clusters in\nthe AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Section 5.1 Provided Interfaces lists the interfaces\nprovided by\nExecution Management\nto other Functional Clusters. Section 5.2 \nRequired Interfaces lists the interfaces required by\nExecution Management\n.\nA detailed technical architecture documentation of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is\nprovided in [6].\n5.1 Provided Interfaces"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P22_33",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P22_34",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "This interface shall be used by the daemon process(es)\ninside\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nto\nreport their execution state to\nExecution Management\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P22_35",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.3: Interfaces required by Execution Management from other Functional Clusters\nFigure 5.3 shows the interfaces required by\nExecution Management\nfrom other\nFunctional Clusters within the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Table 5.2 provides a com-\nplete list of required interfaces from other Functional Clusters within the AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform.\n22 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P23_36",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P23_37",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall use this interface to log\nstandardized messages."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P23_38",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshould use this interface to\nread/write persistent data."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P23_39",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall use this interface to\nenable supervision of its process(es) by\nPlatform\nHealth Management\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P24_40",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02560",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 24,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n6 Requirements Tracing\nThe following tables reference the requirements specified in [5] and links to the fulfill-\nment of these. Please note that if column Satisfied by is empty for a specific require-\nment this means that this requirement is not fulfilled by this document."

      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_58",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_02001] [SWS_EM_02201]\n[SWS_EM_02210] [SWS_EM_02263]\n[SWS_EM_02269] [SWS_EM_02275]\n[SWS_EM_02281] [SWS_EM_02282]\n[SWS_EM_02284] [SWS_EM_02290]\n[SWS_EM_02291] [SWS_EM_02510]\n[SWS_EM_02530] [SWS_EM_02541]\n[SWS_EM_02544]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_59",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nset-up one process for the execution\nof each\nModelled Process\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_60",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_01014] [SWS_EM_01015]\n[SWS_EM_01041] [SWS_EM_01042]\n[SWS_EM_01043]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_61",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nsupport the configuration of OS\nresource budgets for\nprocess\nand\ngroups of\nprocesses\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_62",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_02102] [SWS_EM_02103]\n[SWS_EM_02106] [SWS_EM_02108]\n[SWS_EM_02109]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_63",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nsupport the binding of all threads of a\ngiven process to a specified set of\nprocessor cores."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_64",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\ncontrol the right to create child\nprocesses\nfor each\nprocess\nit\nstarts."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_65",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_01030] [SWS_EM_01033]\n[SWS_EM_02559]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_66",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nsupport multiple instances of\nExecutables\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_67",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_01012] [SWS_EM_01072]\n[SWS_EM_01078] [SWS_EM_02246]\n[SWS_EM_02247] [SWS_EM_02248]\n[SWS_EM_02249]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_68",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nsupport self-initiated graceful\nshutdown of\nprocesses\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_69",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nsupport a Trusted Platform."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_70",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_02299] [SWS_EM_02300]\n[SWS_EM_02301] [SWS_EM_02302]\n[SWS_EM_02303] [SWS_EM_02305]\n[SWS_EM_02306] [SWS_EM_02307]\n[SWS_EM_02308] [SWS_EM_02309]\n[SWS_EM_02556]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_71",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nsupport integrity and authenticity\nmonitoring."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_72",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_02300] [SWS_EM_02301]\n[SWS_EM_02302] [SWS_EM_02303]\n[SWS_EM_02305] [SWS_EM_02306]\n[SWS_EM_02400] [SWS_EM_02556]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_73",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nperform\nMachine\n-wide coordination\nof\nprocesses\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_74",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_01320] [SWS_EM_01321]\n[SWS_EM_01322] [SWS_EM_01325]\n[SWS_EM_01326] [SWS_EM_01327]\n[SWS_EM_01328]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_75",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nprovide APIs to the\nprocess\nfor\nconfiguring external trigger conditions\nfor its activities."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P26_76",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_01304] [SWS_EM_01313]\n[SWS_EM_01320] [SWS_EM_01325]\n[SWS_EM_01326]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P27_77",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01301",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P27_78",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01301",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nprovide APIs to the\nprocess\nfor\nconfiguring cyclic triggering of its\nactivities."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P27_79",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01301",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_EM_01301] [SWS_EM_01302]\n[SWS_EM_01303] [SWS_EM_01304]\n[SWS_EM_01351] [SWS_EM_01352]\n[SWS_EM_01353] [SWS_EM_02201]\n[SWS_EM_02203] [SWS_EM_02210]\n[SWS_EM_02211] [SWS_EM_02215]\n[SWS_EM_02217] [SWS_EM_02510]\n[SWS_EM_02511] [SWS_EM_02512]\n[SWS_EM_02513] [SWS_EM_02514]\n[SWS_EM_02515] [SWS_EM_02520]\n[SWS_EM_02530] [SWS_EM_02531]\n[SWS_EM_02532] [SWS_EM_02533]\n[SWS_EM_02534] [SWS_EM_02535]\n[SWS_EM_02540] [SWS_EM_02550]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P27_80",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01301",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Execution Management\nshall\nprovide APIs to the\nprocess\nto\nsupport deterministic redundant\nexecution of\nprocesses\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P27_81",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01301",

    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P28_96",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02549",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 28,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Table 6.1: RequirementsTracing\n6.1 Not applicable requirements\n[SWS_EM_NA]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThese requirements are not applicable as they are not within\nthe scope of this release.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00111, RS_AP_00115, RS_AP_00125, RS_AP_-\n00133, RS_AP_00135, RS_AP_00136, RS_AP_00137, RS_AP_00141, RS_AP_-\n00142, RS_EM_00151, RS_AP_00156, RS_EM_NA)\n28 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P29_97",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 29,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional specification\nExecution Management\nis a functional cluster contained in the\nAdaptive Plat-\nform Foundation\n.\nExecution Management\nis responsible for all aspects of sys-\ntem execution management including platform initialization and startup / shutdown of\nApplications\n.\nExecution Management\nworks in conjunction with the Operating System. In partic-\nular,\nExecution Management\nis responsible for configuring the Operating System to\nperform run-time scheduling and resource monitoring of\nApplications\n.\nThis chapter describes the functional behavior of\nExecution Management\n.\n•\nSection 7.2 presents an introduction to key terms within\nExecution Manage-\nment\nfocusing on the relationship between\nApplication\n,\nExecutable\n, and\nModelled Process\n. With the latter, we refer to an instance of the meta-model\ndescribing a process, it will eventually be realized by an operating system\npro-\ncess\n.\n•\nSection 7.3 covers the core\nExecution Management\nrun-time responsibilities\nincluding the start of\nApplications\n.\n•\nSection 7.4 describes the lifecycle of\nApplications\nincluding\nModelled Pro-\ncess\nstate transitions and startup / shutdown sequences.\n•\nSection 7.5 covers several topics related to State Management within\nExecu-\ntion Management\nincluding\nFunction Group\nstate management and state\ntransition behavior.\n•\nSection 7.6 documents support provided by\nExecution Management\nDeter-\nministic\nexecution such that given the same input and internal state, a calculation\nwill always produce the same output.\n•\nSection 7.7 describes how\nExecution Management\nsupports resource man-\nagement including the limitation of usage of CPU and memory by an\nApplica-\ntion\n.\n•\nSection 7.8 provides an introduction to Fault Tolerance strategies in general. This\nsection will be expanded in a future release to describe how such strategies are\nrealized within\nExecution Management\n.\n•\nSection 7.9 covers the topic of\nTrusted Platform\n, i.e. ensuring the integrity\nand authenticity of\nApplications\n.\n29 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P30_98",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 30,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.1 Functional Cluster Lifecyle\n7.1.1 Startup\nSee Section 7.5.2.1.\n7.1.2 Shutdown\nSee Section 7.5.2.2.\n7.1.3 Restart\nSee Section 7.5.2.2.\n7.2 Technical Overview\nThis chapter presents a short summary of the relationship between\nApplication\n,\nExecutable\n, and\nModelled Process\n.\n7.2.1 Application\nApplications\nare developed to resolve a set of coherent functional requirements.\nAn\nApplication\nconsists of executable software units, additional execution related\nitems (e.g. data or parameter files), and descriptive information used for integration\nand execution (e.g. a formal model description based on the AUTOSAR meta model,\ntest cases, etc.).\nApplication Executables\ncan be located on user-level above the middleware or\ncan implement functional clusters of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n(located on\nthe level of the middleware), see [constr_1605] in [3].\nIn general, an\nApplication\n, whether user-level or platform-level, is treated the same\nby\nExecution Management\nand can use all mechanisms and APIs provided by the\nOperating System and other functional clusters of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Plat-\nform\n. However in doing so it potentially restricts its portability to other implementations\nof the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n.\n7.2.2 Adaptive Application\nAn\nAdaptive Application\nis a specific type of\nApplication\n. The implementa-\ntion of an\nAdaptive Application\nfully complies with the AUTOSAR specification,\n30 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P31_99",
      "source_element": "SWS_OSI_01001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 31,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\ni.e. it is restricted to the use of APIs standardized by AUTOSAR and needs to follow\nspecific coding guidelines to allow reallocation between different implementations of\nthe\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n.\nAdaptive Applications\nare always located above the middleware. To allow porta-\nbility and reuse, user-level\nApplications\nshould be\nAdaptive Applications\nwhenever technically possible.\nFigure 7.1 shows the different types of Applications."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P32_100",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P32_101",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The Execution Management uses\ncontents of the processed Manifests\nto start up and configure each\npro-\ncess\nindividually."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P32_102",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.2: Executable Lifecycle from deployment to execution\n7.2.4 Modelled Process\nA\nModelled Process\nis an instance of an\nExecutable\n. On the\nAUTOSAR Adap-\ntive Platform\n, a\nModelled Process\nis realized at run-time as an OS process.\nFor details on how\nExecution Management\nstarts and stops\nprocesses\nsee 7.4.\nExecution Management\ntreats all\nExecutables\nand the derived\nModelled Pro-\ncesses\nthe same way, independent of\nApplication\nboundaries.\n32 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P33_103",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nRemark:\nIn this release of this document it is mostly assumed that\nprocesses\nare\nself-contained, i.e. that they take care of controlling thread creation and scheduling\nby calling APIs of the Operating System Interface from within the code.\nExecution\nManagement\nonly starts and terminates the\nprocesses\nand while the\nprocesses\nare running,\nExecution Management\nonly interacts with the\nprocesses\nby pro-\nviding\nState Management\nmechanisms (see 7.5) or APIs to support Deterministic\nExecution (see 7.6.3).\n7.2.5 Execution Manifest\nAn\nExecution Manifest\nis created together with a\nService Instance Mani-\nfest\n(not used by Execution Management) at design time and deployed onto a\nMa-\nchine\ntogether with the\nExecutable\nit is attached to.\nThe\nExecution Manifest\nspecifies the deployment related information of an\nEx-\necutable\nand describes in a standardized way the machine specific configuration\nof\nModelled Process\nproperties (startup parameters, resource group assignment,\nscheduling priorities etc.).\nThe\nExecution Manifest\nis bundled with the actual executable code in order to\nsupport the deployment of the executable code onto the\nMachine\n.\nEach instance of an\nExecutable\nbinary, i.e. each started\nprocess\n, is individually\nconfigurable, with the option to use a different configuration set per\nMachine State\nor per\nFunction Group State\n(see Section 7.5 and [TPS_MANI_01012], [TPS_-\nMANI_01013], [TPS_MANI_01017] and [TPS_MANI_01041]).\nTo perform its necessary actions,\nExecution Management\nimposes a number of\nrequirements on the content of the\nMachine Manifest\nand\nExecution Manifest\n.\nThe validation of the configuration is expected to be done by the vendor tooling.\nFor more information regarding the\nExecution Manifest\nspecification please see\n[3].\n7.2.6 Machine Manifest\nThe\nMachine Manifest\nis also created at integration time for a specific\nMachine\nand is deployed like\nExecution Manifests\nwhenever its contents change. The\nMachine Manifest\nholds all configuration information which cannot be assigned to\na specific\nExecutable\nor its instances (the\nModelled Processes\n), i.e. which is\nnot already covered by an\nExecution Manifest\nor a\nService Instance Mani-\nfest\n.\nThe contents of a\nMachine Manifest\nincludes the configuration of\nMachine\nprop-\nerties and features (resources, safety, security, etc.). For details see [3].\n33 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P34_104",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 34,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.7 Manifest Format\nThe\nExecution Manifests\nand the\nMachine Manifest\ncan be transformed from\nthe original standardized ARXML into a platform-specific format (called\nProcessed\nManifest\n), which is efficiently readable at\nMachine\nstartup. The format transforma-\ntion can be done either off board at integration time or at deployment time, or on the\nMachine\n(by Update and Configuration Management) at installation time.\n34 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P35_105",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01030",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 35,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.3 Execution Management Responsibilities\nExecution Management\nis responsible for all aspects of\nprocess\nexecution man-\nagement. A\nprocess\nis a loaded instance of an\nExecutable\n, which is part of an\nApplication\n.\nExecution Management\nis started as part of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nstartup phase and is responsible for starting and terminating\nprocesses\n.\nExecution Management\ndetermines when, and possibly in which order, to start or\nstop\nprocesses\n, i.e. instances of the deployed\nExecutables\n, based on information\nin the\nMachine Manifest\nand\nExecution Manifests\n.\nExecution Management\nensures that the integrity and authenticity of all\nExecuta-\nbles\nand\nExecutable\n-related data (e.g. manifests) is checked. In the case of a\nfailed integrity or authenticity check,\nExecution Management\ncarries out the mea-\nsures defined in Section 7.9.\n[SWS_EM_01030]\n{OBSOLETE}\nRestriction of process creation right for pro-\ncesses\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall restrict the rights of\nprocesses\nsuch that\nthey cannot start other processes.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00009)\n[SWS_EM_02558]\n{DRAFT}\nDefault value for permissionToCreateChildProcess at-\ntribute\n⌈\nA\nModelled Process\nwithout a specified\npermissionToCreateChild-\nProcess\nattribute shall be considered by\nExecution Management\nas though the\nattribute was set to false.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\n[SWS_EM_02559]\n{DRAFT}\nRestriction of process creation right for processes\n⌈\nIf\npermissionToCreateChildProcess\nattribute is false then\nExecution Manage-\nment\nshall restrict the rights of the created process such that it cannot start / create\nother processes.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00009)\nThe mechanism by which the restriction of [SWS_EM_02559] is implementation-\nspecific, but could be realized by configuring the process capability attribute mask at\nthe time of process creation (OS feature).\nPlease note that when setting\npermissionToCreateChildProcess\nto true, the in-\ntegrator should consider several aspects:\n•\nthe safety and security implications of this configuration. Does this software come\nfrom a trusted source? Is this configuration absolutely necessary for the software\nto fulfill its task? etc.\n•\nthe process that creates child processes is responsible for termination of pro-\ncesses that it creates; processes not started by\nExecution Management\nare not controlled by\nExecution Management\nand exist outside of\nAUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n.\n•\nthe system resources used by the child processes are generally unplanned. It is\nrecommended to assign the parent to a dedicated\nResourceGroup\nto limit the\nimpact on memory and CPU usage.\n35 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P36_106",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01050",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 36,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nDepending on the\nMachine State\nor on any other\nFunction Group State\n, de-\nployed\nExecutables\nare started during\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nstartup or\nlater, however it is not expected that all will begin active work immediately since many\nprocesses\nwill provide services to other\nprocesses\nand therefore wait and listen\nfor incoming service requests.\nExecution Management\nderives an ordering for startup/shutdown of deployed\nExe-\ncutables\nwithin the context of Machine and/or Function Group State changes based\non declared\nExecution Dependencies\n[SWS_EM_01050]. The dependencies are\ndescribed in the\nExecution Manifests\n, see [TPS_MANI_01041].\nExecution Management\nis\nnot\nresponsible for run-time scheduling of\nprocesses\nsince this is the responsibility of the Operating System [SWS_OSI_01003]. How-\never,\nExecution Management\nis responsible for initialization / configuration of the\nOS to enable it to perform the necessary run-time scheduling and resource manage-\nment based on information extracted by\nExecution Management\nfrom the\nMachine\nManifest\nand\nExecution Manifests\n.\nExecution Management\ndoes not perform standardized termination handling - the\nresponse to receipt of a signal, e.g.\nSIGTERM\n, by\nExecution Management\nis there-\nfore implementation defined.\n7.3.1 Error handling\nAll API operations can potentially raise errors.\n[SWS_EM_02547] Obtain error information\n⌈\nAccording to Adaptive Platform Core\n[4],\nExecution Management\nshall provide means to obtain information about errors\nthat occurred during API calls. For that reason,\nExecution Management\ncan return\nthe following errors:\n•\nara::exec::ExecErrc\n[SWS_EM_02281]\n•\nara::exec::ExecException\n[SWS_EM_02282]\n•\nara::exec::ExecException::ExecException\n[SWS_EM_02283]\n•\nara::exec::ExecErrorDomain\n[SWS_EM_02284]\n•\nara::exec::ExecErrorDomain::ExecErrorDomain\n[SWS_EM_02286]\n•\nara::exec::ExecErrorDomain::Name\n[SWS_EM_02287]\n•\nara::exec::ExecErrorDomain::Message\n[SWS_EM_02288]\n•\nara::exec::GetExecErrorDomain\n[SWS_EM_02290]\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00150)\n36 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P37_107",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02548",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 37,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_EM_02548] Create error information\n⌈\nAccording to Adaptive Platform Core\n[4],\nExecution Management\nshall provide means to create error information as listed\nbelow.\n•\nara::exec::ExecErrorDomain::ThrowAsException\n[SWS_EM_02289]\n•\nara::exec::MakeErrorCode\n[SWS_EM_02291]\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00150)\n37 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P38_108",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02000",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 38,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4 Process Lifecycle Management\n7.4.1 Execution State\nExecution States\ncharacterizes the internal lifecycle of a\nprocess\n. In other words, they\ndescribe it from the point of view of a\nprocess\nthat is executed. The states visible to\nthe\nprocess\nare defined by the\nara::exec::ExecutionState\nenumeration, see\n[SWS_EM_02000]."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P38_109",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02000",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 38,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.3: Execution States\nThe Execution State of a\nprocess\nis used by\nExecution Management\nto construct\nand maintain the\nProcess State\nas described in Section 7.4.2. Execution State\nchange notifications from a\nprocess\nresult in\nProcess State\nchanges managed\nby\nExecution Management\n. The Execution State and\nProcess State\nare main-\ntained separately so that there is no explicit dependency between a\nprocess\n's Ex-\necution State and\nExecution Management\n's\nProcess State\n. This allows future\nevolution of\nProcess State\nwithout impacting the internal Execution State of the\nprocess\n.\n7.4.1.1 Initialization\n[SWS_EM_01401] ExecutionClient usage restriction\n⌈\nThe\nAUTOSAR Adaptive\nPlatform\nimplementation shall only allow a\nprocess\nto report its own Execution-\nState.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\nExecution Management\nconsiders\nprocess\ninitialization complete when the\nPro-\ncess State Running\nis reached whether this is achieved implicitly (by a\nNon-re-\nporting Process\n) or explicitly through a\nprocess\nreporting its Execution State.\nA\nprocess\nis required (see [SWS_EM_01004]) to report\nkRunning\nstate using the\nara::exec::ExecutionClient::ReportExecutionState\n[SWS_EM_02003]\nmethod of class\nara::exec::ExecutionClient\n, see [SWS_EM_02001]. It would\ntypically report after the completion of its initialization, but before\nService Discov-\nery\nis completed. If the\nprocess\nwere to report\nkRunning\nonly after\nService Dis-\ncovery\ncompletion, the non-deterministic delays may impact other\nprocesses\n, due\nto delays in resolution of\nExecution Dependencies\n.\n38 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P39_110",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01055",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 39,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.1.2 Termination\n[SWS_EM_01055] Initiation of process termination\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall initiate\nprocess\ntermination by sending the\nSIGTERM\nsignal to the\nprocess\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\nNote that from the perspective of\nExecution Management\n, requirement\n[SWS_EM_01055] only requests the initiation of the steps necessary for grace-\nful termination under the control of the\nprocess\n.\nIt is possible that a process that should be terminated according to [SWS_EM_01055],\ne.g. during the handling of\nExecution Dependencies\n, is no longer alive. However,\nas\nExecution Management\ncan determine the status of child processes it would\nthus not attempt to terminate a process that no longer exists.\nExecution Management\nmay send\nSIGTERM\nat any time, even before the\nprocess\nhas reported\nkRunning\nstate and thus the\nprocess\nis still in the\nInitializing\nProcess State\n.\nOn receipt of\nSIGTERM\n, a\nprocess\ncommences the actual termination.\nExecution Management\nprovides a termination handler to minimize the required\nsignal handling in the\nAdaptive Application\n(see [SWS_EM_02577]).\n[SWS_EM_02577]\n{DRAFT}\nCall of Termination Handler\n⌈\nOn receipt of\nSIGTERM\nara::exec::ExecutionClient\nshall invoke the termination handler defined by\nara::exec::ExecutionClient::Create\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\nPlease note the API defines the execution context of the termination handler to be a\nbackground thread which is maintained by the\nara::exec::ExecutionClient\n. It\nis not executed in a signal handler context, therefore usage of POSIX and\nara\nAPIs is\nnot restricted (potential restrictions in the contract of\nara\nAPIs still apply).\nDuring the\nTerminating\nstate, the\nprocess\nis expected to save persistent data and\nfree all internally used resources. The\nprocess\nindicates completion of the\nTermi-\nnating\nstate by termination with exit status 0 (\nEXIT_SUCCESS\n).\nExecution Management\nas the parent\nprocess\ncan detect termination of the child\nprocess\nand take the appropriate platform-specific actions such as processing exe-\ncution dependencies that rely on the\nTerminated\nstate and thus ensure that there is\nno overlap between these\nprocesses\nwhen both are running.\n[SWS_EM_01314] Default value for\nterminationBehavior\n⌈\nExecution Man-\nagement\nshall treat a\nModelled Process\nwithout specified\nterminationBehav-\nior\nas a\nprocess\nthat terminates only on request by\nExecution Management\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\n39 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P40_111",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01309",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 40,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.1.3 Unexpected Termination\n[SWS_EM_01309]\nUnexpected Termination\nof a\nprocess\n⌈\nIn case of\nUnex-\npected Termination\noutside a state transition resulting from previous request from\nara::exec::StateClient::SetState\n,\nExecution Management\nshall perform\nthe following actions:\n1. log event, if logging is activated\n2. Set the\nFunction Group State\n(of the\nFunction Group\nto which the rel-\nevant\nModelled Process\nwas mapped) to\nUndefined Function Group\nState\n.\n3. Call\nundefinedStateCallback\ndefined by\nara::exec::StateClient\nwith\nara::exec::ExecutionErrorEvent\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\nIf the\nState Management\ndecides to invoke the\nara::exec::StateClient::\nGetExecutionError\ninterface, after receiving the\nundefinedStateCallback\n[SWS_EM_01309] or inside the callback, the\nara::exec::ExecutionErrorEvent\nwill contain the same information as provided by the\nundefinedStateCallback\n. This is\nguaranteed by [SWS_EM_02542]. Please note that [SWS_EM_01309] also applies\nfor\nUnexpected Self-termination\n.\nCorrect\nExecution State\nreporting performed by\nprocesses\nis a part of consistent\nbehavior of\nExecution Management\n.\n7.4.1.4 Application Reporting\n[SWS_EM_02243] Handling Execution State Running\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall return\nkInvalidTransition\nwhen a\nprocess\nreports Execution State\nkRun-\nning\n(using the method\nara::exec::ExecutionClient::ReportExecution-\nState\n) and the\nprocess\nis not in\nProcess State Starting\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\nTo prevent denial-of-service attacks on\nExecution Management\nan implementation\ncould rate-limit acceptance of Execution State reports or could request the Operating\nSystem to terminate the underlying process. However such reactions are not standard-\nized.\nExecution Management\ndifferentiates between two types of\nprocesses\n:\nReport-\ning Processes\nand\nNon-reporting Processes\n.\nReporting Processes\nare\nconsidered to be the normal form of\nprocesses\nand\nNon-reporting Processes\nare considered to be an exception.\nNon-reporting Processes\ncan be used to support running\nExecutables\nwhich\nhave not been designed with the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nin mind. For exam-\nple, if an\nExecutable\nis available as binary only, if it is not feasible to patch its source\ncode or if the\nExecutable\nis only used during development time.\n40 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P41_112",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01402",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 41,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe implicit transition to\nRunning Process State\nis described by [SWS_EM_01402]\nIn safety related systems the system designer has to use\nNon-reporting Process\nfunctionality with care. Such\nprocesses\nwill probably not provide safety critical func-\ntionality and will not be monitored by\nPlatform Health Management\nbut still they\nmight influence other safety related\nprocesses\nand therefore can introduce a safety\nrisk. To isolate\nNon-reporting Processes\nfrom safety critical parts\nResource-\nGroup\ncan be used (see Section 7.7).\nAn attempt to report\nExecution State\nby a\nNon-reporting Process\nis considered\nan error by\nExecution Management\n.\n[SWS_EM_01403] Reporting Non-reporting Process\n⌈\nara::exec::Execution-\nClient::ReportExecutionState\nshall treat it as a Violation when invoked by a\nNon-reporting Process\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\n7.4.2 Process States\nProcess States\ncharacterize the lifecycle of a\nprocess\nfrom the point of view of\nExecution Management\n. In other words,\nProcess States\nrepresent the\nExe-\ncution Management\ninternal tracking of the\nExecution States\n(see Section 7.4.1)\nand hence there is no need for a standardized type. Note that each\nprocess\nis in-\ndependent and therefore has its own\nProcess State\n.\nProcess State\nis used by\nExecution Management\nto resolve Execution Dependencies, manage timeouts, etc.\nAdditionally to the existing values for the\nProcess State\n(\nIdle\n,\nStarting\n,\nRun-\nning\n,\nTerminating\n,\nTerminated\n), the implementation may define its own\nProcess\nStates\n, which are not in conflict/not replacing the existing ones."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P41_113",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01402",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 41,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.4: process Lifecycle\n[SWS_EM_01002] Idle Process State\n⌈\nThe\nIdle Process State\nshall be the\nProcess State\nprior to creation of the\nprocess\nand to resource allocation.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nEM_00103)\n[SWS_EM_01003] Starting Process State\n⌈\nThe\nStarting Process State\nshall\napply when the\nprocess\nhas been created and resources have been allocated.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nEM_00103)\n[SWS_EM_01004] Running Process State of Reporting Processes\n⌈\nThe\nRunning\nProcess State\nshall apply to a\nReporting Process\nafter it has reported\nkRun-\nning\nExecution State to\nExecution Management\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\n41 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P42_114",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01402",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 42,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_EM_01402] Implicit Running Process State\n⌈\nFor\nNon-reporting Process\nthe transition from\nStarting\nto\nRunning Process State\nshall implicitly apply after\nExecution Management\nhas allocated the required resources and created the run-\ntime process.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\n[SWS_EM_01404] Terminating Process State after Termination Request\n⌈\nThe\nTerminating Process State\nshall apply when\nExecution Management\nsent\nSIGTERM\nsignal to the\nprocess\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103, RS_EM_00011)\n[SWS_EM_01006] Terminated Process State\n⌈\nThe\nTerminated Process State\nshall apply after the\nprocess\nhas terminated and the\nprocess\nresources have been\nfreed.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103, RS_EM_00011)\nFor [SWS_EM_01006],\nExecution Management\nobserves the exit status of all\npro-\ncesses\n. The mechanism is implementation dependent but could, for example, use the\nPOSIX\nwaitpid()\nAPI.\nFrom the resource allocation point of view, the\nTerminated Process State\nis sim-\nilar to the\nIdle Process State\n there is no\nprocess\nrunning and no resources\nare allocated. However from the execution point of view, the\nTerminated Process\nState\nis different from\nIdle\nas it tells\nExecution Management\nthat the\nprocess\nhas already been executed, terminated and can be now restarted (if needed) as spec-\nified in [SWS_EM_01066]. The distinction between\nProcess State Idle\nand\nTer-\nminated\nis relevant for resolving\nExecution Dependencies\nto\nSelf-terminat-\ning Processes\n(see Section 7.4.4.1).\n7.4.2.1 Synchronization with Platform Health Management\nPlatform Health Management\nrequires\nProcess State\ninformation for starting\nand stopping of Supervisions. For details see [8].\nPlatform Health Management\nneeds the information that a Supervised\nprocess\nreported Execution State\nkRunning\n([SWS_EM_01004]) to start Alive Supervision.\n[SWS_EM_01210] Report kRunning received event to Platform Health Manage-\nment\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall inform\nPlatform Health Management\nif a\nSupervised\nprocess\nhas reported Execution State\nkRunning\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\nPlatform Health Management\nneeds the information that termination of a Super-\nvised\nprocess\nwill be initiated ([SWS_EM_01055]) to stop Intra-process Supervisions.\n[SWS_EM_01211] Report initiating process termination event to Platform\nHealth Management\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall inform\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nwhen a Supervised\nprocess\ntermination is about to be initiated.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nEM_00103)\nPlatform Health Management\nneeds the information that a Supervised\nprocess\nis terminated ([SWS_EM_01006]) to supervise\nSelf-terminating Processes\n.\n42 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P43_115",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01212",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 43,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_EM_01212] Report process terminated event to Platform Health Man-\nagement\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall inform\nPlatform Health Management\nwhen a Supervised\nprocess\nis terminated.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\nHint: Which\nprocesses\nare Supervised by\nPlatform Health Management\ncan\nbe determined by referring to the configuration of\nPlatform Health Management\n.\nThe above notifications are provided through Inter-Functional Cluster Interface(s) be-\ntween\nExecution Management\nand\nPlatform Health Management\n. As such\ninterfaces are vendor-specific, their definition (signature) is not standardized.\nIf\nExecution Management\nis used in Safety Critical Platform, then it is suggested to\nuse Alive/Logical/Deadline supervision(s) and report their checkpoints appropriately to\nPlatform Health Management\n.\n7.4.3 Trace Process State Transitions\nThe timing behavior of\nprocesses\nis a mandatory part of the lifecycle of an\nAppli-\ncation\n. Wrong timing and timing shortages in\nprocesses\ncan lead to unexpected\nbehavior or failures. Therefore it is important to provide a way to trace\nprocess\nlifetime\nevents within the\nExecution Management\n. The following trace points are introduced\nto be able to do a timing analysis of an\nApplication\nbased on its\nprocesses\n.\n[SWS_EM_02573]\n{DRAFT}\nState Transition logging  process created\n⌈\nWhenever\nExecution Management\nhas created a process (see [SWS_EM_01003]),\nExecu-\ntion Management\nshall log a DltMessage of type\nProcessCreated\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_-\n00152)\n[SWS_EM_02574]\n{DRAFT}\nState Transition logging  process kRunning re-\nceived\n⌈\nWhenever\nExecution Management\nhas received a kRunning (see\n[SWS_EM_02003]),\nExecution Management\nshall log a DltMessage of type\nPro-\ncessKRunningReceived\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00152)\n[SWS_EM_02575]\n{DRAFT}\nState Transition logging  process termination re-\nquest\n⌈\nWhenever\nExecution Management\nis requesting a process to be terminated\n(see [SWS_EM_01055]),\nExecution Management\nshall log a DltMessage of type\nProcessTerminationRequest\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00152)\n[SWS_EM_02576]\n{DRAFT}\nState Transition logging  process terminated\n⌈\nWhenever a process terminates (independent of a success return result),\nExecution\nManagement\nshall log a DltMessage of type\nProcessTerminated\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00152)\n43 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P44_116",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 44,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.4 Startup and Termination\n7.4.4.1 Execution Dependency\nExecution Management\ncan derive an ordering for the startup and termination of\nprocesses\nwithin\nState Management\nframework based on the declared\nExecu-\ntion Dependencies\n. This ensures that\nApplications\nare started before depen-\ndent\nApplications\nuse the services that they provide and, likewise, that\nApplica-\ntions\nare shutdown only when their provided services are no longer required.\nThe\nExecution Dependencies\n, see [TPS_MANI_01041] and [constr_1606], are\nconfigured in the\nExecution Manifests\n, which is created at integration time based\non information provided by the\nApplication\ndeveloper. An\nExecution Depen-\ndency\ndefines the provider of functionality required by a\nprocess\nnecessary for that\nprocess\nto provide its own functionality.\nExecution Management\nensures the de-\npendent\nprocesses\nare in the state defined by the\nExecution Dependency\nbefore\nthe\nprocess\ndefining the dependency is started.\nUser-level\nApplications\nare expected to use the service discovery mechanisms of\nCommunication Management\nas the primary mechanism for execution sequencing\nas this is supported both within a\nMachine\nand across\nMachine\nboundaries. Thus\nuser-level applications should not rely on\nExecution Dependencies\nunless strictly\nnecessary. Which\nprocesses\nare running depends on the current\nFunction Group\nStates\n, including the\nMachine State\n, see Section 7.5. The integrator should en-\nsure that all service dependencies are mapped to the State Management configuration,\ni.e. that all dependent\nprocesses\nare running when needed.\nIn real life, specifying a simple dependency to a\nprocess\nmight not be sufficient to\nensure that the depending service is actually provided. Since some\nprocesses\nshall\nreach a certain\nExecution State\n(see Section 7.4.1) to be able to offer their services to\nother\nprocesses\n, the dependency information shall also refer to\nProcess State\nof\nthe\nprocess\nspecified as dependency. With that in mind, the dependency information\nmay be represented as a pair like:\n<process>.<processState>\n. For more details\nregarding the\nProcess States\nrefer to Section 7.4.2.\nThe following dependency use-cases have been identified:\nDependency on\nRunning\nProcess State\nIn case\nprocess\nB has a simple depen-\ndency on\nprocess\nA, the\nRunning Process State\nof\nprocess\nA is specified\nin the dependency section of\nprocess\nB's\nExecution Manifest\n.\nWhen\nprocess\nB has a\nRunning Execution Dependency\nto\nprocess\nA,\nthen\nprocess\nB will only be started once the\nprocess\nA achieves\nRunning\nProcess State\n.\nDependency on\nTerminated\nProcess State\nIn case\nprocess\nD depends on\nSelf-terminating Process\nC, the\nTerminated Process State\nof\npro-\ncess\nC is specified in the dependency section of\nprocess\nD's\nExecution\nManifest\n.\n44 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P45_117",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_CONSTR_00001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIf\nprocess\nD has\nTerminated Execution Dependency\non\nprocess\nC, then\nprocess\nD will only be started once\nprocess\nC reaches the\nTerminated\nstate.\nA\nTerminated Execution Dependency\nspecified on a non self-terminating\nprocess\nis considered to be a configuration error as this would indi-\ncate a dependency that can only be fulfilled at the next group transition\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_00001]\nNote:\nNo use-case has been identified for an\nExecution Dependency\non other\nProcess States\n, i.e.\nIdle\nor\nTerminating\n, and therefore these are not supported\nfor\nExecution Dependency\nconfiguration. See also [SWS_EM_CONSTR_01744].\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_01744]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of process state in the context of\nthe\nExecutionDependency\n⌈\nThe target\nModeDeclaration\nreferenced in the role\nExecutionDependency\n.\nprocessState\nshall fulfill the following conditions:\n•\nIt shall be owned by a\nModeDeclarationGroup\nthat is referenced by a\nMod-\neDeclarationGroupPrototype\n(in the role\ntype\n) that in turn shall be aggre-\ngated by a\nProcess\n.\n•\nThe\nshortName\ns of the encapsulated\nModeDeclaration\ns shall only be one of\nthe following values:\n\nRunning\n\nTerminated\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00100)\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_00001]\n{DRAFT}\nModeling execution dependency for the\nTerminated\nstate\n⌈\nA\nTerminated ModeDeclaration\nreferenced in the\nPro-\ncess\n.\nstateDependentStartupConfig\n.\nexecutionDependency\nshall only be al-\nlowed if the process referenced in the\nstateDependentStartupConfig\n.\nexecu-\ntionDependency\nhas\nStartupConfig\n.\nterminationBehavior\nset to\nproces-\nsIsSelfTerminating\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00100)\nExample 7.1\nConsider a\nprocess\n,\nDataLogger\n, which has an\nExecution Dependency\non an-\nother\nprocess\n,\nStorage\n. For startup this means\nDataLogger\nhas a\nExecution De-\npendency\non\nStorage\nso the latter is required to be started by\nExecution Manage-\nment\nbefore\nDataLogger\nso that\nDataLogger\ncan store its data.\nprocesses\nare only started by\nExecution Management\nif they reference a re-\nquested\nMachine State\nor\nFunction Group State\n, but not because of config-\nured\nExecution Dependencies\n.\nExecution Dependencies\nare only used to\ncontrol a startup or terminate sequence at state transitions. Note that the scope of\nEx-\necution Dependency\nresolution is limited to one\nFunction Group State\nonly\n(see [constr_1689] and [SWS_EM_02245]).\n45 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P46_118",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01050",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_EM_01050] Start Dependent processes\n⌈\nDuring startup of a\nprocess\n,\nEx-\necution Management\nshall respect\nExecution Dependencies\nby ensuring that\neach\nprocess\nupon which the\nprocess\nto be started depends have reached its re-\nquested\nProcess State\n(at some previous point in time) during the current state\ntransition before starting the\nprocess\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00100)\nThe same\nExecution Dependencies\nused to define the startup order are also used\nto define the termination order. However the situation is reversed as\nExecution Man-\nagement\nis required to ensure that dependent\nprocesses\nare terminated\nafter\nthe\nprocess\nto ensure that the services required remain available until no longer required.\n[SWS_EM_01051] Termination of processes\n⌈\nDuring termination of a\nprocess\n,\nEx-\necution Management\nshall respect\nExecution Dependencies\nby ensuring that\neach\nprocess\nupon which the\nprocess\nto be terminated depends is not terminated\nbefore termination of the\nprocess\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00100)\nExample 7.2\nConsider the same\nprocess\n,\nDataLogger\n, as above which has an\nExecution De-\npendency\non another\nprocess\n,\nStorage\n. For termination the\nExecution Depen-\ndency\nindicates\nExecution Management\nis required to only terminate\nStorage\nafter\nDataLogger\nso the latter can flush its data during termination.\nNote that [SWS_EM_01051] merely requires\nExecution Management\nto not termi-\nnate the dependent\nprocesses\nbefore terminating a\nprocess\n. It is not an error if the\nprocess\nhas self-terminated so is not available to be terminated.\nIf no\nExecution Dependencies\nare specified between two\nprocesses\nthen no\norder is imposed and they can be started or terminated in an arbitrary order.\nExample 7.3\nConsider three\nprocesses\n:\n•\nStorage\n, a service\nprocess\nwithout any dependencies;\n•\nStorageConsistencyChecker\n, a self-terminating\nprocess\n, it requires\nStorage\nto\nbe in\nProcess State Running\n;\n•\nConf igReader\n, a service\nprocess\n, it requires that the\nStorageConsistencyChecker\nhas reached\nProcess State Terminated\n;\nFor startup this means\nExecution Management\nshould start\nStorage\nand\nwait till it reports\nkRunning\n, then\nExecution Management\nshould start\nStorageConsistencyChecker\nand wait till it terminates and only then start\nConf igReader\n. For termination the\nExecution Dependency\nindicates that\nExe-\ncution Management\ncan terminate\nStorage\nand\nConf igReader\nsimultaneously be-\ncause\nStorageConsistencyChecker\nis already terminated and\nConf igReader\ndoes not\nhave a direct dependency on\nStorage\n. If\nConf igReader\nhas to be terminated before\n46 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
