      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P47_119",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01050",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 47,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nStorage\n, then this can be achieved by adding a direct\nExecution Dependency\nbe-\ntween\nConf igReader\nand\nStorage\n.\nThe required dependency information is provided by the\nApplication\ndeveloper. It\nis adapted to the specific\nMachine\nenvironment at integration time and made available\nin the\nExecution Manifest\n.\nExecution Management\nparses the information and uses it to build the startup se-\nquence to ensure that the required antecedent\nprocesses\nhave reached a certain\nProcess State\nbefore starting a dependent\nprocess\n[SWS_EM_01050].\n[SWS_EM_01001] Execution Dependency error\n⌈\nIf\nExecution Management\nneeds to start\nprocess\nA that depends on another\nprocess\nB and\nprocess\nB is\nnot part of the same\nFunction Group State\nas\nprocess\nA, then Execution Man-\nagement shall consider this as an Error and fail to start\nprocess\nA.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00100)\nExample 7.4\nLet assume that\nprocess\nA depends on the\nRunning Process State\nof a\npro-\ncess\nB. At a\nMachine State\ntransition,\nprocess\nA shall be started, because it\nreferences the new\nMachine State\n. However,\nprocess\nB does not reference that\nMachine State\n, so it is not started. Due to the\nExecution Dependency\nbetween\nthe two\nprocesses\n,\nprocess\nA would never start running in the new\nMachine\nState\nbecause it waits forever for\nprocess\nB. This is considered to be a configura-\ntion error and shall also cause run time error.\nPlease note that requirement [SWS_EM_01001] effectively forbids any\nExecution\nDependencies\nthat spans outside of a single\nFunction Group State\n(or a\nMa-\nchine State\n) definition, see also [constr_1689]. This is done on purpose, as\nthis kind of dependencies will introduce hidden dependencies between\nFunction\nGroups\nand they will not be visible to\nState Management\n. If dependencies be-\ntween\nFunction Groups\nneed to be expressed (e.g. mapping software could have\ndependency on GPS software), then this should be done inside\nState Management\n.\nFor more information see [9].\nUnlike a\nReporting Process\n, a\nNon-reporting Process\nis in\nProcess State\nRunning\ndirectly after start. Regardless of whether the process has completed its\ninitialization phase and is ready to offer its services or not. This means that\nRunning\nExecution Dependencies\nare immediately satisfied and thus do not achieve the\noriginal semantics when specified for a\nNon-reporting Processes\nwithout further\naction.\nThis limitation can be overcome by introducing a\nCompanion Process\n, which acts\nas a representative of the\nNon-reporting Process\n. The\nCompanion Process\nwaits for availability of the service provided by the\nNon-reporting Process\nand\nreports\nkRunning\nto\nExecution Management\n. The\nprocesses\nwhich in fact need\nthe services of the\nNon-reporting Process\ncan be configured to be dependent on\n47 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthe\nCompanion Process\n. Please note that the\nTerminated Execution Depen-\ndency\nis not affected as\nExecution Management\nis informed by the\nOperating\nSystem\nwhen\nNon-reporting Processes\nare\nTerminated\n. Please see Figure\n7.5 for more details."

    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P48_121",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01402",

      "source_page": 48,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.5: Execution dependencies on Non-reporting Process\n•\nNon-reporting Process\n(and\nSelf-terminating Process\n)\nA\nrefer-\nences\nFG1:Running\n. This process is started first (as it doesn't have any\nExecu-\ntion Dependencies\nconfigured) and automatically enters\nRunning\nProcess\nState\nas per [SWS_EM_01402].\n•\nCompanion Process\nB\nis started after\nNon-reporting Process\nA\n(please\nnote that\nA\nand\nB\nare also standard AUTOSAR\nprocesses\n) enter\nRunning\nstate.\nprocess\nB\ncan use project specific method to assess if\nprocess\nA\nis\nfully functional and signal this to\nExecution Management\nby reporting (or not)\nkRunning\nstate.\n48 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P49_122",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01055",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 49,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n•\nprocess\nC\nis started when (and only when)\nprocess\nB\nenters\nRunning\nPro-\ncess State\n(i.e. reports\nkRunning\n). Please note this\nExecution Depen-\ndency\nwill work independently from reporting / non-reporting configuration of\nprocess\nC\n.\n•\nprocess\nD\nhas\nTerminated\nExecution Dependency\nconfigured on\nSelf-\n-terminating Process\n(and\nNon-reporting Process\n)\nA\n. As mentioned\nearlier this works out of the box (no special action needed here).\n7.4.4.2 Signal Mask\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nis defining a POSIX based system for\nApplica-\ntions\n- this includes POSIX signals. Signal handling is not a trivial task. Therefore\ninteraction with POSIX signals is limited to a necessary minimum in\nAUTOSAR Adap-\ntive Platform\n. The only reason for POSIX signal interaction is\nExecution Man-\nagement\n's\nprocess\ntermination request (see [SWS_EM_01055]).\nExecution Management\nstarts\nprocesses\nwith a well defined signal mask to avoid\nthe situation of threads having an undefined signal mask (e.g. threads created by\nara\n).\n[SWS_EM_02578]\n{DRAFT}\nInitial signal mask for Reporting Process\n⌈\nExecution\nManagement\nshall start\nReporting Processes\nwith a signal mask having all POSIX\nsignals blocked except of:\n•\nSIGABRT\n•\nSIGBUS\n•\nSIGFPE\n•\nSIGILL\n•\nSIGSEGV\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\nThe set of unblocked POSIX signals provided in [SWS_EM_02578] are raised by the\nOS when an error occurs where there is no reasonable way to continue program exe-\ncution. According to POSIX, ignoring these signals would lead to undefined behavior.\nIf one of these signals occurs, the default signal handling action, in this case abnor-\nmal termination, is performed. Note also that the two POSIX signals\nSIGSTOP\nand\nSIGKILL\ncannot be caught or blocked.\nAdaptive Application\nmake use of\nara::exec::ExecutionClient\nwhich im-\nplements catching the\nSIGTERM\nsignal (see [SWS_EM_02577]).\nNon-reporting Processes\nwon't use the\nara::exec::ExecutionClient\nand\nwill implement their own signal handling. For such\nApplications Execution Man-\nagement\nprepares an empty signal mask.\n49 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P50_123",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02579",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 50,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_EM_02579]\n{DRAFT}\nInitial signal mask for Non-Reporting process\n⌈\nExe-\ncution Management\nshall start\nNon-reporting Processes\nwith an empty signal\nmask.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00103)\n7.4.4.3 Arguments\nExecution Management\nprovides argument passing for a\nprocess\ncontaining\none or more\nStateDependentStartupConfig\nin the role\nProcess\n.\nstateDepen-\ndentStartupConfig\n. This permits different\nprocesses\nto be started with different\narguments.\n[SWS_EM_01012] Process Argument Passing\n⌈\nAt the initiation of startup of a\npro-\ncess\n, the aggregated\nProcessArgument\nof the\nStartupConfig\nreferenced by the\nStateDependentStartupConfig\nshall be passed to the\nprocess\nby\nExecution\nManagement\nbased on [SWS_EM_01072] and [SWS_EM_01078].\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00010)\nNote that [SWS_EM_01012] deliberately does not specify the OS mechanism used to\nstart a\nprocess\n, e.g. the\nexec\n-family based POSIX interface, as this is ultimately an\nimplementation specific property.\nThe first argument passed by\nExecution Management\nis the name of the\nExe-\ncutable\n.\n[SWS_EM_01072] process Argument Zero\n⌈\nArgument 0 shall be set to name of the\nExecutable\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00010)\nExecution Management\nsupports passing arguments to a\nprocess\nin the same\nway that a shell passes command line arguments to a POSIX process.\nExecu-\ntion Management\nassigns each\nProcessArgument\n.\nargument\nto an element in\nthe\nargv[]\narray, starting at element index 1, and passes this to the\nprocess main()\nfunction.\nProcessArgument\nordering is used to preserve the semantics of an\n(op-\ntion, argument)\npair such as \n-b value\n, where the \n-b\n argument must precede\nthe \nvalue\n argument. This method supports the short form and long form argument\npassing conventions typically used in POSIX environments.\n[SWS_EM_01078] Process Argument strings\n⌈\nProcessArgument\n.\nargument\nshall\nbe passed to the\nprocess\nin order with the first\nProcessArgument\n.\nargument\nstart-\ning at Process Argument 1.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00010)\nThe order in which the defined\nProcessArgument\nare passed is defined by the or-\ndered\nStartupConfig\n.\nprocessArgument\naggregation.\n7.4.4.4 Environment Variables\nExecution Management\ninitializes environment variables for\nprocesses\n.\nprocess\nspecific environment variables are configured in its\nExecution Manifest\n.\nMachine\n50 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P51_124",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02246",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 51,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nspecific environment variables are configured in the\nMachine Manifest\n. During run-\ntime environment variables are accessible via POSIX\ngetenv()\ncommand.\n[SWS_EM_02246] process specific Environment Variables\n⌈\nExecution Manage-\nment\nshall prepare environment variables based on the configuration from\nProcess\n.\nstateDependentStartupConfig\n.\nstartupConfig\n.\nenvironmentVariable\nand\npass them during a\nprocess\nstart.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00010, RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_EM_02247] Machine specific Environment Variables\n⌈\nExecution Man-\nagement\nshall prepare environment variables based on the configuration from\nMa-\nchine\n.\nenvironmentVariable\nand pass them during a\nprocess\nstart.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_-\n00010, RS_AP_00130)\nPlease note that AUTOSAR meta model (see [3]) uses\nTagWithOptionalValue\nfor\nenvironment variables definition ([TPS_MANI_01208] and [TPS_MANI_01209]). As\nexplained there, the value (\nTagWithOptionalValue\n.\nvalue\n) can be omitted as a\nway of specifying environment variable with empty value.\n[SWS_EM_02249] Missing value from Environment Variable definition\n⌈\nWhenever\nExecution Management\nfinds environment variable definition, that has\nTagWith-\nOptionalValue\n.\nvalue\nmissing, it should use empty string as a value for this envi-\nronment variable.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00010, RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_EM_02248] Environment Variables precedence\n⌈\nWhenever the same envi-\nronment variable is configured within both the\nExecution Manifest\nand the\nMa-\nchine Manifest\nthen\nExecution Management\nshall use the environment variable\nvalue from the\nExecution Manifest\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00010, RS_AP_00130)\n7.4.5 Machine Startup Sequence\nExecution Management\nis the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n's first process.\nWhen ready,\nExecution Management\ninitiates the\nMachine State\ntransition\nfrom the\nOff\nstate (the default state before EM is started) to the\nStartup\nstate\n([SWS_EM_01023], [SWS_EM_02250]). During the transition,\nExecution Manage-\nment\nrequests startup of processes that exist in the\nStartup Machine State\n.\nAfter the necessary state transition conditions have been met (see Section 7.5.5\nand 7.5.2.1),\nExecution Management\nreports\nMachine State Startup\ntransition\nconfirmation to\nState Management\n([SWS_EM_02241]). At that point,\nExecution\nManagement\nhands over responsibility for\nFunction Group\nstate management (i.e.\ninitiation of state change requests) to\nState Management\n.\nOn a\nMachine\n, which can be any group of resources, i.e. a physical environment, a\nvirtualized environment over a hypervisor, or an OS-level virtualization (container),\nEx-\necution Management\nis not necessarily the first process launched; Other processes\nneeded by the system may exist, such as an\nOperating System\ninit process, or an\nOperating System\nMicro-kernel user-level processes like drivers, filesystem, etc.\n51 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P52_125",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01000",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 52,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nAll of these processes might be started and managed outside of the context of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n.\nPlease note that an\nApplication\nconsists of one or more\nExecutables\n. There-\nfore to launch an\nApplication\n,\nExecution Management\nstarts\nprocesses\nas\ninstances of each\nExecutable\n.\n[SWS_EM_01000] Startup order\n⌈\nThe startup order of the platform-level\nprocesses\nshall be determined by\nExecution Management\nbased on\nMachine Manifest\nand\nExecution Manifest\ninformation.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00100)\nPlease see Section 7.2.5.\nFigure 7.6 shows the overall startup sequence."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P53_126",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 53,

    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P54_127",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_CONSTR_02556",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 54,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.5 State Management\n7.5.1 Overview\nState Management\nfunctional cluster defines the operational state of an\nAUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n, while\nExecution Management\nperforms the transitions be-\ntween different states.\nThe\nExecution Manifest\nallows to define in which states the\nModelled Pro-\ncesses\nhave to run (see [3]). As mentioned before, a\nModelled Process\nis an\ninstance of an\nExecutable\n, which is part of an\nApplication\n.\nState Manage-\nment\nmechanisms grant full control over the set of\nApplications\nto be executed\nand ensures that\nprocesses\nare only executed (and hence resources allocated) when\nactually needed.\nFour different states are relevant for\nExecution Management\n:\nExecution State\n An Execution States characterizes the internal lifecycle of each\nstarted\nprocess\n, see Section 7.4.1\nProcess State\n\nProcess States\nare managed by an\nExecution Management\ninternal state machine. For details see Section 7.4.2.\nMachine State\n see Section 7.5.2\nFunction Group State\n see Section 7.5.3\nAn example for the interaction between these states will be shown in section Section\n7.5.4.\n7.5.2 Machine State\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_02556]\n{DRAFT}\nMandatory states\n⌈\nExecution Manage-\nment\nrequires that at least one\nFunction Group\nwith the name\n\"MachineFG\"\nis\nconfigured for each\nMachine\n. This\nFunction Group\nhas several mandatory states:\n•\nOff\n,\n•\nVerify\n,\n•\nStartup\n,\n•\nShutdown\n, and\n•\nRestart\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nIn order to clarify the required contents of the \"MachineFG\" function group and its\ntype, the ARXML model AUTOSAR_MOD_GeneralDefinition_MachineFG.arxml (avail-\nable in MOD_GeneralDefinitions) provides a definition.\n54 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P55_128",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02263",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 55,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nAdditional\nMachine States\ncan be defined on a machine specific basis and are\ntherefore not standardized.\nThe\nExecution Manifest\ndefines the relation between processes and\nFunction\nGroup States\n. Therefore it is possible to determine the set of executed processes for\neach\nFunction Group State\n. A\nFunction Group State\nis modeled by means\nof\nModeDeclaration\n, see [TPS_MANI_03145] and [TPS_MANI_03194].\nIn the API, a\nFunction Group\nis represented by the class\nara::exec::Func-\ntionGroup\n, see [SWS_EM_02263] and a\nFunction Group State\nby the class\nara::exec::FunctionGroupState\n, see [SWS_EM_02269]. Class\nara::exec::\nStateClient\nperforms state management during the lifetime of a\nMachine\n, see\n[SWS_EM_02275].\nMachine States\n(as well as other\nFunction Group States\n) are requested by\nState Management\n. The set of active states is significantly influenced by vehicle-\nwide events and modes. For details on state change management see Section 7.5.5.\n[SWS_EM_01032] Machine States configuration\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall\nobtain the configuration of\nMachine States\nfrom\nFunction Group \"MachineFG\"\nwithin the\nSoftwareCluster\nwith category\nPLATFORM_CORE\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_02557]\n{DRAFT}\nScope of machine Function Group\n⌈\nThe function-Group that represents the Machine Function Group group (see\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_02556]) shall only be referenced in the role claimedFunction-\nGroup by a\nSoftwareCluster\nof category\nPLATFORM_CORE\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nPlease note that according to [constr_1788] there must be exactly one\nSoft-\nwareCluster\nwith category\nPLATFORM_CORE\non each machine.\nThe start-up sequence from initial state\nStartup\nto the point where\nState Manage-\nment\n,\nSM\n, requests the initial running machine state\nStateXYZ\nis illustrated in Figure\n7.8.\n55 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P56_129",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 56,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P56_130",

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.8: Start-up Sequence  from\nStartup\nto initial running state\nStateXYZ\nA successful Function Group state change sequence is illustrated in Figure 7.9. Here,\non receipt of the state change request,\nExecution Management\nterminates running\nprocesses\nand then starts\nprocesses\nactive in the new state before confirming the\nstate change to\nState Management\n.\n56 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"

      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P59_134",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02250",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 59,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.11: State Change Sequence - Start-up Timeout\nThere are more cases which lead to failure during Function Group state change, which\nare not illustrated here. For details see chapter 7.5.5 \"State Transition\" and chapter\n8.2.7.8 \"StateClient::SetState\".\n7.5.2.1 Startup\n[SWS_EM_02250]\n{DRAFT}\nMachine State Startup\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall\nenter\nUnrecoverable State\nif\nExecution Management\nis not able to parse the\nStartup\nstate information of\nFunction Group \"MachineFG\"\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nExecution Management\ndepends on the existence of a\nStartup\nstate\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_02556]. However, at run time the state may not be available\nto\nExecution Management\nfor a number of reasons (e.g. misconfigured develop-\nment system, corrupted file system, memory errors etc.). While these situations may\nnot be common, to avoid implementation specific behavior,\nExecution Management\nshould have standardized reaction to them.\n[SWS_EM_01023] Self initiation of Machine State Startup transition\n⌈\nExecution\nManagement\nshall self initiate the state transition to the\nStartup Machine State\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n59 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P60_135",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02555",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 60,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nPlease note that for\nMachine State\ntransitions, the requirements of section Section\n7.5.5 apply.\n[SWS_EM_02555]\n{DRAFT}\nFailure in Machine State Startup transition\n⌈\nExecu-\ntion Management\nshall enter\nUnrecoverable State\nin the event of failed transi-\ntion to the\nStartup Machine State\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nA failure in transition to\nStartup Machine State\nis considered as a serious prob-\nlem. In that event\nExecution Management\ncan't be sure what level of functionality is\navailable and if a failed state transition can be handled by\nState Management\n. It is\nworth to note that the\nState Management\nitself can be unavailable or its functionality\ncan be very limited at that point in time.\n[SWS_EM_02241] Machine State Startup Completion\n⌈\nUpon completion of initial\n(self initiated)\nMachine State\ntransition to the\nStartup\nstate,\nExecution Man-\nagement\nshall make the result of that transition available to\nState Management\nthrough\nara::exec::StateClient::GetInitialMachineStateTransition-\nResult\nAPI.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nPlease note that the notification in [SWS_EM_02241] is not done via broadcast mes-\nsage but has to be requested by\nState Management\nvia the\nara::exec::State-\nClient::GetInitialMachineStateTransitionResult\nAPI.\nThe function\nara::exec::StateClient::GetInitialMachineStateTransi-\ntionResult\nretrieves the result of the Machine State's initial transition to the Startup\nstate. After the Startup state is reached (as described by [SWS_EM_02241])\nExecu-\ntion Management\ndoes not initiate any further\nFunction Group State\nchanges\n(this includes\nMachine State\n). Instead such changes are requested by\nState\nManagement\nand then performed by\nExecution Management\n.\nExecution Management\nwill be controlled by other software entities and should\nnot execute any\nFunction Group State\nchanges on its own (with one exception:\n[SWS_EM_01023]). This creates some expectations towards system configuration.\nThe specification expects that\nState Management\nwill be configured to run in ev-\nery\nMachine State\n(this includes\nStartup\n,\nShutdown\nand\nRestart\n) [SWS_SM_-\nCONSTR_00001]. Above expectation is needed in order to ensure that there is always\na software entity that can introduce changes in the current state of the\nMachine\n. If\n(for example) system integrator doesn't configure\nState Management\nto be started\nin\nStartup Machine State\n, then\nMachine\nwill never be able transit to any other\nstate and will be stuck forever in it. This also applies to any other\nMachine State\nthat doesn't have\nState Management\nconfigured.\nThe possibility that the\nMachine State\ntransition to the\nStartup\nstate is never\nreached shall be taken into account. In this case the\nState Management\ncan\ninterrupt the\nStartup\nstate transition and request e.g. a recovery state using\nthe\nara::exec::StateClient::SetState\ninterface. The\nara::exec::State-\nClient::GetInitialMachineStateTransitionResult\nwould return the value\nkCancelled\n.\n60 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P61_136",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02241",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 61,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.5.2.2 Shutdown/Restart\nExecution Management\ndoes not perform shutdown/restart of the\nMachine\nto\navoid embedding project-specific behavior within\nExecution Management\n. Instead\na project-specific actor is expected to provide a mechanism to shutdown/restart the\nMachine\n, such as, a standalone process that is configured to be started by\nExecu-\ntion Management\nduring transition to the\nShutdown\n/\nRestart Machine State\nor a process started in\nStartup Machine State\nthat waits for a signal before shut-\nting down the\nMachine\n. This approach enables the control of both WHEN and HOW\nshutdown/restart occurs to be managed in a project-specific manner. See [3] [constr_-\n1618] and [constr_1619].\nRequirements [SWS_EM_02241] and [SWS_EM_01023] dictate a dependency by\nExecution Management\non the presence of the\nStartup Machine State\nand\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_02556] mandates configuration of\nStartup\nand\nShutdown\n/\nRestart Machine States\n. However there is no equivalent requirement on\nShut-\ndown\nor\nRestart Machine States\nas their omission does not prevent\nExecution\nManagement\nfrom starting. Therefore, the response by\nExecution Management\nto\nthis misconfiguration is implementation-specific.\nA request to\nExecution Management\nto change the current\nMachine State\nto\neither Shutdown or Restart is handled the same as any other\nFunction Group\nstate\nchange request. From the point of view of\nExecution Management\nall\nFunction\nGroup\ns are independent and therefore changes to them, can be applied without any\nside effects.\nHowever, from the point of view of\nState Management\n, where knowledge of the de-\npendencies between different Function Groups exist this may not be true. AUTOSAR\nassumes that\nState Management\nwill requests\n\"MachineFG\"\nShutdown or Restart\nwhen it's valid to do so; see [9] for advice on how to orchestrate shutdown of the\nMachine\n.\nPlease note it is system integrator's responsibility to carefully consider when system\nshutdown / restart should be requested because all\nprocesses\nwhich are still running\nwill not be terminated by\nExecution Management\n, which means that they will not be\nable to persist their data.\nAs mentioned in Section 7.5.2.1, AUTOSAR assumes that\nState Management\nwill\nbe configured to run in Shutdown and Restart. State transition is not a trivial system\nchange and it can fail for a number of reasons - in which case\nState Management\nshould remain alive to report errors and wait for further instructions. Please note that\nthe purpose of entering the Shutdown or Restart state is to shutdown or restart the\nMachine\n(this includes\nState Management\n) in a clean manner.\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_02558]\n{DRAFT}\nAbility to shut down\n⌈\nIn the context of one\nMachine\n, at least one\nProcess\nshall have a\nstateDependentStartupConfig\n.\nfunctionGroupState\nthat has the\nshortName Shutdown\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n61 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P62_137",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_CONSTR_02559",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 62,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_EM_CONSTR_02559]\n{DRAFT}\nAbility to restart\n⌈\nIn the context of one\nMachine\n, at least one\nProcess\nshall have a\nstateDependentStartupConfig\n.\nfunctionGroupState\nthat has the\nshortName Restart\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02549]\n{DRAFT}\nMachineFG.Off handling\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall refuse a request to change\n\"MachineFG\" Function Group State\nto\nOff\nwith error\nkInvalidTransition\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n7.5.3 Function Group State\nIf there is a group of\nApplications\ninstalled on the machine, it will be useful to have\nability of controlling them coherently. For that very reason the concept of\nFunction\nGroups\nwas introduced to\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n.\nEach\nFunction Group\nhas its own set of\nprocesses\nand set of states called\nFunc-\ntion Group States\n. Each\nFunction Group State\ndefines which\nprocesses\nshall be started when\nState Management\nrequests\nFunction Group State\nacti-\nvation from\nExecution Management\n.\nThe\nFunction Groups\nmechanism is very flexible and is intended as a tool used to\nstart and stop\nprocesses\nof\nApplications\n. System integrator can assign\npro-\ncesses\nto a\nFunction Group State\nand then request it by\nState Management\n.\nFor details on state change management see Section 7.5.5.\nA\nModelled Process\nmay not be assigned to more than one\nFunction Group\n[constr_1688]. To see why this constraint is required consider the contrary a\nModelled\nProcess\nmapped to two states in two\nFunction Groups\n. The\nModelled Process\nis now running in the two states and a\nFunction Group State\ntransition in either\nstate would require the\nprocess\nto be terminated. This termination would violate the\nintegrity of the second\nFunction Group State\nand hence the constraint exists to\nprevent this situation.\nIn general,\nMachine States\n(see Section 7.5.2) are used to control machine lifecy-\ncle (startup/shutdown/restart) and\nprocesses\nof platform level\nApplications\n, while\nother\nFunction Group States\nindividually control\nprocesses\nwhich belong to\ngroups of user-level\nApplications\n. Please note that this doesn't mean that all\npro-\ncesses\nof platform level\nApplications\nhave to be controlled by\nMachine States\n.\nFigure 7.12 shows an example of state change sequence where several\npro-\ncesses\nreference\nMachine States\nand\nFunction Group States\nof two addi-\ntional\nFunction Groups\nFG1\nand\nFG2\n. For simplicity, only the three static\nProcess\nStates Idle\n,\nRunning\n, and\nTerminated\nare shown for each process.\n62 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P63_138",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",

    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P64_139",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01107",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 64,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nSystem design and integration should ensure that enough resources are available on\nthe machine at any time, i.e. the added resource consumption of all\nprocesses\nwhich\nreference simultaneously active states should be considered.\n[SWS_EM_01107]\n{OBSOLETE}\nFunction Group configuration\n⌈\nExecution Man-\nagement\nshall obtain configuration of the\nFunction Group\nfrom the\nProcessed\nManifest\nto set-up the\nFunction Group\nspecific state management.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_-\n00101)\nA proper system configuration requires that each\nprocess\nreferences in its\nEx-\necution Manifest\none or more\nFunction Group States\n(which can be\nMa-\nchine States\n) of the same\nFunction Group\n. If a\nprocess\ndoesn't reference any\nFunction Group States\nit will never be started, for more details please refer to\n[SWS_EM_01066] and chapter 7.5.5 State Transition.\n[SWS_EM_01013]\n{OBSOLETE}\nFunction Group State\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall support the execution of a specific\nModelled Process\n, depending on the cur-\nrent\nFunction Group State\nand on information provided in the\nExecution Man-\nifests\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nEach\nModelled Process\nis assigned to one or several startup configurations (\nStar-\ntupConfig\n), which each can define the startup behavior in one or several\nFunction\nGroup States\n(including\nMachine States\n). For details see [3]. By parsing this\ninformation from the\nExecution Manifests\n,\nExecution Management\ncan de-\ntermine which\nModelled Processes\nneed to be launched if a specific\nFunction\nGroup State\nis entered, and which startup parameters are valid.\n[SWS_EM_01033] process start-up configuration\n⌈\nTo enable a\nModelled Pro-\ncess\nto be launched in multiple\nFunction Group States\n,\nExecution Manage-\nment\nshall be able to configure the\nprocess\nstarted on every\nFunction Group\nState\nchange based on information provided in the\nExecution Manifest\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nEM_00009, RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02254]\n{OBSOLETE}\nMisconfigured process - assigned to more than\none Function Group\n⌈\nDuring a\nFunction Group State\ntransition, any\nprocess\ninvolved that references states from more than one\nFunction Group\n, shall cause\nEM to perform following actions:\n1. Stop the\nFunction Group State\ntransition, so\nState Management\ncan de-\ncide how to proceed.\n2. Log event if needed\n3. Set the current\nFunction Group State\nto\nUndefined Function Group\nState\n.\n4. Report\nkFailed\nin the\nara::exec::StateClient::SetState\ninterface to\nindicate that the State change request cannot be fulfilled.\n5. Report the\nexecutionError\nconfigured for requested\nFunction Group\nState\nvia the\nara::exec::StateClient::GetExecutionError\ninterface.\n64 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P65_140",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01110",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 65,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nPlease note AUTOSAR doesn't support the possibility of assigning a single\nprocess\nto more than one\nFunction Group\n, see [3] ([constr_1688]).\n[SWS_EM_01110] Off States\n⌈\nEach\nFunction Group\n(including the\nFunction\nGroup \"MachineFG\"\n) has an\nOff\nState which shall be used by\nExecution Man-\nagement\nas initial\nFunction Group State\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nWithin any FunctionGroup, including\n\"MachineFG\"\n, the \nOff\n state is mandatory as\nthe initial state [TPS_MANI_03195] and cannot have\nModelled Processes\nmapped\naccording to [constr_3424]. [SWS_EM_01110] and [SWS_EM_01023] together define\nthe very first\nFunction Group\nstate transition after the power up.\nprocesses\nreference in their\nExecution Manifest\nthe states in which they want\nto be executed. A state can be any\nFunction Group State\n, including a\nMachine\nState\n. For details see [3], especially \"State-dependent Startup Configuration\" chapter\nand \"Function Groups\" chapter.\nThe arbitrary state change sequence as shown in Figure 7.9 applies to state changes\nof any\nFunction Group\n- just replace\n\"MachineFG\"\nby the name of the\nFunction\nGroup\n. On receipt of the state change request,\nExecution Management\nterminates\nno longer needed\nprocesses\nand then starts\nprocesses\nactive in the new\nFunc-\ntion Group State\nbefore confirming the state change to\nState Management\n. For\ndetails see Section 7.5.5.\n7.5.4 State Interaction\nFigure 7.13 shows a simplified example for the interaction between different types of\nstates, after\nState Management\nfunctional cluster has requested different\nFunc-\ntion Group States\n. One can see the state transitions of the\nFunction Group\nand the process and Execution States of one\nprocess\nwhich references one state\nof this\nFunction Group\n, ignoring possible delays and dependencies if several\npro-\ncesses\nwere involved.\n65 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P66_141",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02298",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 66,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P66_142",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02298",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 66,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.13: Interaction between states\n7.5.5 State Transition\nState Management\ncan request to change one or several\nFunction Group\nStates\n(including the\nMachine State\n), using API described in Section 8.2.7.\nara::\nexec::StateClient::SetState\nallows\nState Management\nto request several\nFunction Group State\nchanges in parallel. If\nMachine State\nchange is re-\nquired, the name of the\nFunction Group\npassed shall be:\n\"MachineFG\"\n.\n[SWS_EM_02298] Request of a state transition different to the state that the\nFunction Group\nis already in transition to\n⌈\nAfter successful validation of a\nara::\nexec::StateClient::SetState\ncall for a\nFunction Group\nthat is already un-\nder state transition,\nExecution Management\nshall cancel the ongoing\nFunction\n66 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P67_143",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02296",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 67,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nGroup State\ntransition (and set that request's\nara::core::Future\nto\nkCan-\ncelled\n) before starting the new\nFunction Group State\ntransition (and returning\na new\nara::core::Future\nfor the new request).\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02296] Request of a state transition to a state that the\nFunction\nGroup\nis already in transition to\n⌈\nAfter successful validation of a\nara::exec::\nStateClient::SetState\ncall for a\nFunction Group\nthat is already under state\ntransition,\nExecution Management\nshall:\n•\nset the\nara::core::Future\nof the previous request to\nkCancelled\nif there is\none\n•\nreturn a new\nara::core::Future\nfor the new request\n•\ncontinue the ongoing\nFunction Group\nstate transition\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nThere is only one situation where a transition to a state could be performed without a\nprevious request. When\nExecution Management\nis performing the initial transition\nto\n\"MachineFG\"\nstartup [SWS_EM_01023], State Management can decide to request\na different state of\n\"MachineFG\"\n. In this situation there is no previous request, so\nthere is no\nara::core::Future\n, that can be set to\nkCancelled\n.\nBefore\nExecution Management\ncancels an ongoing request according to\n[SWS_EM_02298] or [SWS_EM_02296] the new request should be assessed as valid,\nthis includes, but is not limited to, [SWS_EM_02549].\nPlease note that [SWS_EM_02298] merely ensures that\nExecution Management\nfirst informs the requester of the ongoing transition (instance of\nara::exec::State-\nClient\n) about the cancellation, before informing the new requester that the new re-\nquest has been accepted. Both requesters could be the same instance of\nara::\nexec::StateClient\n.\n[SWS_EM_02295] Request of a state transition to a state that the\nFunction\nGroup\nis already in\n⌈\nara::exec::StateClient::SetState\nshall ignore the re-\nquest and return immediately with success.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nNote that an error domain value is not used for [SWS_EM_02295] as this would be\ninterpreted as an error by State Management and thus trigger the associated error\nhandling.\nThere are no other requirements or assumtions on order in which requests from\nara::\nexec::StateClient::SetState\nare processed.\nRequesting the same\nFunction Group State\nlike before (independently if the pre-\nvious state request is already finished or still ongoing) shall be prevented, because it\nmight lead to unwanted execution dependencies. When the same\nFunction Group\nState\nis to be requested again another state has to be requested before. Please\nnote that\nState Management\ncan repeat state transition request (to the same state)\n67 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P68_144",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 68,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nif previous transition ended with error. This is allowed because a failed state transition\nis considered as invalid\nFunction Group State\n.\nSince\nExecution Management\nallows a new\nara::exec::StateClient::Set-\nState\ncall to interrupt an ongoing transition and thus change the destination\nFunc-\ntion Group State\nof the transition, it may happen (especially in misconfigured sys-\ntem, or during the development phase) that some of\nara::exec::StateClient::\nSetState\nrequests will be issued by mistake. It is in the best interest of\nExecution\nManagement\nto inform requester (instance of\nara::exec::StateClient\n) of the\nongoing transition, that it had been canceled by a newer request as soon as possible."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P69_145",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 69,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nof a single\nFunction Group State\ndefinition are forbidden, as they would result in\nstarting a\nprocess\nthat is not configured to run in the given\nState\n. For more informa-\ntion on\nExecution Dependencies\nsee chapter Section 7.4.4.1 ([SWS_EM_01001]\nand [constr_1689]).\nPlease note that\nprocess\nB\nhas different\nExecution Dependencies\nin\nFunc-\ntion Group State\nABC and\nFunction Group State\nXYZ. This configuration\nrequires existence of two different startup configurations (\nStateDependentStar-\ntupConfig\n), which in turns will mandate\nprocess\nB\nrestart if\nState Management\nrequest\nFunction Group State\nchange from ABC to XYZ. This is enforced by\n[SWS_EM_02251].\nFrom the above we can conclude that each\nFunction Group\nis a separate entity\nand state transition of one\nFunction Group\ndoesn't have side effects on another\nFunction Group\n. Please note that this is true from the point of view of\nExecution\nManagement\nand may differ from the point of view of\nState Management\n(see [9] if\nyou need more information on this).\nIn the following requirements the\nExecution Manifest\nof a\nModelled Process\nis the formal modelling of\nprocess\nstartup behaviour and is implemented by means\nof the aggregation of meta-class\nStateDependentStartupConfig\nin the role\nPro-\ncess\n([TPS_MANI_01012]).\nThe term \"the\nprocess\nreferences a\nState\n\" indicates a\nfunctionGroupState\nthat\nreferences an instance of\nStateDependentStartupConfig\nwithin the\nStartup-\nConfig\nthat is applicable for the\nprocess\nassociated with the specific\nFunction\nGroup State\n.\nCurrentState\nis the current (currently active)\nState\nof a\nFunction Group\nfor\nwhich the state transition was requested; or the current\nMachine State\nif the\nFunc-\ntion Group\nhas\n\"MachineFg\"\nname. In short this is a\nFunction Group State\nor\nMachine State\n.\nRequestedState\nis the state that will become the\nCurrentState\n, once the state\ntransition finishes successfully.\nIn other words\nCurrentState\nis the starting point of the transition, the list of the\npro-\ncesses\nthat should be currently running inside the\nFunction Group\n(please note the\nexistence of\nSelf-terminating Processes\n).\nRequestedState\nis a destination\npoint of the state transition, the list of the\nprocesses\nthat will be running inside of\nthe\nFunction Group\nonce the state transition finishes successfully (please note the\nexistence of\nSelf-terminating Processes\n).\nStartupConfig\nis a\nStateDependentStartupConfig\nthat is aggregated in the\nrole\nProcess\n.\nstateDependentStartupConfig\nfor a given\nprocess\n.\nState transition is a complicated process, however it is composed out of three simple\nlogical steps:\n•\nTerminate all\nprocesses\nthat are currently running and are not needed in the\nRequestedState\n69 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P70_146",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01060",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 70,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n•\nRestart all\nprocesses\nthat are currently running and have\nStartupConfig\nthat\ndiffers between the\nCurrentState\nand the\nRequestedState\n•\nStart all\nprocesses\nthat are not running currently and are needed in the\nRe-\nquestedState\nPlease see Section 7.4.1 and Section 7.4.2 for more detail information on how\nExe-\ncution Management\nhandles termination and start of\nprocesses\n(restart is a se-\nquence of termination and start).\n[SWS_EM_01060] State transition - termination behavior\n⌈\nOn state transition\nEx-\necution Management\nshall request termination ([SWS_EM_01055]) of each\npro-\ncess\nthat references the\nCurrentState\nin its\nExecution Manifest\n, but does not\nreference the\nRequestedState\nand has a\nProcess State\ndifferent than\n[\nIdle\nor\nTerminated\n]\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02251] State transition - restart behavior\n⌈\nOn state transition\nExecu-\ntion Management\nshall terminate all\nprocesses\nthat reference the\nCurrentState\nin its\nExecution Manifest\n, but references the\nRequestedState\nwith different\nStartupConfig\nand have\nProcess State\ndifferent than\n[\nIdle\nor\nTerminated\n]\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nPlease note that [SWS_EM_02251] only request a termination of\nprocesses\n, the start\npart will fall under [SWS_EM_01066] requirement thus making the restart complete.\nExecution Management\nmonitors the time required by each\nprocess\nto terminate.\nThe default value of the\nprocess\ntermination timeout is defined by the system inte-\ngrator in the\nMachine Manifest\n, see [TPS_MANI_03151]. This value may be over-\nwritten in the startup configuration of individual\nprocesses\nby defining the termination\ntimeout parameter in the\nExecution Manifest\n, see [TPS_MANI_01278].\n[SWS_EM_01065] State transition - process termination timeout monitoring\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall monitor the time required by the\nprocess\nto termi-\nnate (the time needed by the\nprocess\nto reach the\nTerminated Process State\n).\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02255] State transition - process termination timeout reaction\n⌈\nIn\nthe event of a\nprocess\ntermination timeout (defined by configuration\nStartupCon-\nfig\n.\ntimeout\n),\nExecution Management\nshall request the\nOperating System\nto\nforcibly terminate the underlying process.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nOn multi-process POSIX platforms, this could be achieved using a\nSIGKILL\nsignal.\n[SWS_EM_02258] State transition - process termination timeout reporting\n⌈\nWhen\nthe termination of a\nprocess\nresulted in the timeout,\nExecution Management\nshall\nlog the event, if logging is activated.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nExecution Management\ncontinues a state-transition even in the presence of non-\nterminating processes, since the target\nFunction Group State\nwill be reached as\nthese processes will be killed (see [SWS_EM_02255] and [SWS_EM_01060]). Con-\ntinuing in case of a timeout on termination assures in particular, that the\nFunction\n70 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nGroup State\n\"Off\" can always be reached (provided that a process termination on\nOS level is always successful).\nThis is different in case of processes that timeout during start-up (see\n[SWS_EM_02259]): these processes cannot be forced to start and the\nFunction\nGroup State\nwill not be reached.\n[SWS_EM_01066] State transition - start behavior\n⌈\nOn state transition\nExecution\nManagement\nshall start all\nprocesses\nthat references the\nRequestedState\nin its\nExecution Manifest\nand have\nProcess State\nthat is\n[\nIdle\nor\nTerminated\n]\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nExecution Management\nmonitors the time required by each\nprocess\nto start. The\nstart-up timeout is defined per\nprocess\nstartup configuration by the system integrator\nin the\nExecution Manifest\n, see [TPS_MANI_01277].\n[SWS_EM_02253] State transition - process start-up timeout monitoring\n⌈\nExe-\ncution Management\nshall monitor the time required by the\nprocess\nto start-up (the\ntime between\nExecution Management\nrequesting process creation from the operat-\ning system and the\nprocess\nsuccessfully reporting the\nRunning Process State\n).\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nExecution Management\nmonitors the time required by each\nprocess\nto start. The\nvalue of the\nprocess\nstart-up timeout is defined by the system integrator in the\nExe-\ncution Manifest\n, see [TPS_MANI_01277]. Please note that startup time for\nNon-\n-reporting Processes\nis zero because\nNon-reporting Processes\nimmedi-\nately switch from\nProcess State Idle\nto\nRunning\nskipping the\nStarting\nstate.\n[SWS_EM_02260] State transition - process start-up timeout reaction\n⌈\nIn the event\nof a\nprocess\nstart-up timeout (defined by configuration\nStartupConfig\n.\ntime-\nout\n),\nExecution Management\nshall attempt to restart the\nprocess\nup to\nnum-\nberOfRestartAttempts\ntimes.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nprocess\nstart-up timeout is caused by a malfunction and therefore\nExecution Man-\nagement\nrequests termination of the\nprocess\nby the operating system (e.g. using\nSIGKILL\n) rather than requesting termination through\nSIGTERM\nas the\nprocess\nis\nassumed to be in an erroneous state.\n[SWS_EM_02280] Effect on Execution Dependency\n⌈\nA restart attempt according to\n[SWS_EM_02260] shall not fulfill any terminated dependencies.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02310] State transition - process termination after start-up timeout re-\naction\n⌈\nIn case a\nprocess\nstart-up timeout occurred after\nExecution Management\nattemted to restart the\nprocess numberOfRestartAttempts\ntimes,\nExecution\nManagement\nshall request the\nOperating System\nto terminate the underlying\npro-\ncess\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02259] State transition - process start-up timeout reporting\n⌈\nWhen\nthe start-up of a\nprocess\nresulted in the timeout,\nExecution Management\nshall\nperform following actions:\n71 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.15: Dependency resolution during state change\n[SWS_EM_02245] Dependency resolution during state change\n⌈\nExecution\nManagement\nshall perform\nExecution Dependency\nresolution against the\npro-\ncesses\nthat are configured for\nRequestedState\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nPlease note that [SWS_EM_02245] doesn't bring new functionality to state transition.\nIt merely ensures that [SWS_EM_02251] and [SWS_EM_01066] are performed on\nprocess\nA, before [SWS_EM_01066] is performed on\nprocess\nB. If this order is\nnot ensured then [SWS_EM_02245] could not be satisfied as\nprocess\nA will be a\nprocess\nthat is configured for\nCurrentState\nand not for\nRequestedState\n.\nDescription of\nFunction Group State\ntransition in this chapter may give impres-\nsion that, it is required to first stop all\nprocesses\nthat are not needed in\nRequested-\nState\n, before you can start any of the\nprocesses\nthat are needed. Please note that\nthis is not the case. Step by step approach of this chapter was chosen to introduce as\n73 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nmuch clarity as possible, when describing\nFunction Group State\ntransition. Imple-\nmenters are free to parallelize as much steps (needed for state transition) as possible\nfor a particular implementation.\nExecution Management\nconsiders a state transition has been performed success-\nfully when the following have occurred:\n•\nDependency resolution ([SWS_EM_02245]) has identified\nprocesses\nto\nstart/stop\n•\nAll\nprocesses\nexpected to terminate have terminated ([SWS_EM_01060])\n•\nAll started ([SWS_EM_01066]) or restarted [SWS_EM_02251])\nReporting\nProcesses\nhave reported\nkRunning\n.\n[SWS_EM_01067] Actions on Completion State Transition\n⌈\nOn successful comple-\ntion of a state transition,\nExecution Management\nshall set the\nCurrentState\nto\nthe\nRequestedState\nand report success back to\nState Management\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_-\n00101)\n[SWS_EM_02313]\n{OBSOLETE}\nUnexpected Termination\nof starting\npro-\ncesses\nduring\nFunction Group State\ntransition\n⌈\nIn case of\nUnexpected\nTermination\nduring\nprocess\nstartup ([SWS_EM_01066]),\nExecution Manage-\nment\nshall perform the following actions:\n1. Stop the\nFunction Group State\ntransition, so\nState Management\ncan de-\ncide how to proceed.\n2. log event, if logging is activated\n3. Set the\nCurrentState\nto\nUndefined Function Group State\n.\n4. Report\nkFailedUnexpectedTerminationOnEnter\nin the\nara::exec::\nStateClient::SetState\ninterface to indicate that the State change request\ncannot be fulfilled.\n5. Report the configured\nexecutionError\nvia the\nara::exec::State-\nClient::GetExecutionError\ninterface.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02315]\nUnexpected Termination\nof\nprocesses\nconfigured for the\nRequestedState\nduring a\nFunction Group State\ntransition\n⌈\nIn case of Unex-\npected Termination of a process configured for the\nRequestedState\n,\nExecution\nManagement\nshall perform the following actions:\n1. Stop the\nFunction Group State\ntransition, so\nState Management\ncan de-\ncide how to proceed.\n2. log event, if logging is activated\n3. Set the\nCurrentState\nto\nUndefined Function Group State\n.\n74 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4. Report\nkFailedUnexpectedTermination\nin the\nara::exec::State-\nClient::SetState\ninterface to indicate that the State change request cannot\nbe fulfilled.\n5. Return the configured executionError via the\nara::exec::StateClient::\nGetExecutionError\ninterface.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nPlease note that [SWS_EM_02313] also applies to\nUnexpected Self-termina-\ntion\n.\n[SWS_EM_02314]\n{OBSOLETE}\nUnexpected Termination\nof terminating\npro-\ncesses\nduring\nFunction Group State\ntransition\n⌈\nIn case of\nUnexpected\nTermination\nduring\nprocess\ntermination ([SWS_EM_01060],[SWS_EM_02251]),\nExecution Management\nshall log the event, if logging is activated.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\n[SWS_EM_02316]\nUnexpected Termination\nof a\nprocess\nnot configured for\nthe\nRequestedState\nduring a\nFunction Group State\ntransition\n⌈\nIn case of\nUnexpected Termination\nof a\nprocess\nnot configured for the\nRequestedState\nduring a\nFunction Group State\n,\nExecution Management\nshall continue the\nFunction Group State\ntransition and log the event, if logging is activated.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nEM_00101)\nIf\nprocess\nB depends on the termination of\nprocess\nA during a\nFunction Group\nState\ntransition (this means that both are configured for the\nRequestedState\n), the\ntransition fails if\nprocess\nA dies unexpectedly before reaching the\nTerminated\npro-\ncess state ([SWS_EM_02315]).\nHowever if a process is only configured for the\nCurrentState\nand it dies unexpect-\nedly during the\nFunction Group State\ntransition, then this doesn't stop the\nFunc-\ntion Group State\ntransition. The\nUnexpected Termination\nis logged and nor-\nmal state transition activities are resumed ([SWS_EM_02316]). The reason to continue\nthe transition is twofold:\n•\nThe\nprocess\nwas already marked to be terminated by\nExecution Manage-\nment\n(it was not configured for the\nRequestedState\n). It is irrelevant from the\nState Management point of view if it terminated as expected or due to an internal\nerror.\n•\nTransition to the\nOff\nstate is always guaranteed to be successful and can be\nused as a reaction to an error condition.\n[SWS_EM_02297] StateClient usage restriction\n⌈\nStateClient\nAPI shall treat it as\na Violation when invoked by a\nprocess\nwith\nProcess\n.\nfunctionClusterAffili-\nation\nconfigured to anything else than STATE_MANAGEMENT.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00101)\nIf not protected\nStateClient\ncan be used to destabilise\nMachine\n, see Section 8.2.7\nfor more details.\n75 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"

    {

      "source_page": 76,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.6 Deterministic Execution\n7.6.1 Determinism"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P77_154",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 77,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.6.1.1 Time Determinism\nEach time a calculation is started, its results are guaranteed to be available before\na specified deadline. To achieve this, sufficient and guaranteed computing resources\n(processor time, memory, service response times etc.) should be assigned to the\nsoftware entities that perform the calculation. For more information on resources see\nchapter 7.7.\nNon-deterministic best-effort\nprocesses\ncan request guaranteed minimum re-\nsources for basic functionality, and additionally can have maximum resources specified\nfor monitoring purposes. However, if Time Determinism is requested, the resources\nmust be guaranteed at any time, i.e. minimum and maximum resources are identical.\nIf the assumptions for deterministic execution are violated, e.g. due to a deadline miss,\nthis is an error detectable by the Application. In non-deterministic best-effort subsys-\ntems such deadline violations or other deviations from normal behavior sometimes can\nbe tolerated and mitigated without dedicated error management.\nFully-Deterministic behavior additionally requires Data Determinism, however in many\ncases Time Determinism is sufficient.\n7.6.1.2 Data Determinism\nFor Data Determinism, each time a calculation is started, its results only depend on the\ninput data. For a specific sequence of input data, the results always need to be exactly\nthe same, assuming the same initial internal state.\nA common approach to verify Data Determinism in a safety context is the use of\nlockstep mechanisms, where execution is done simultaneously through two different\npaths and the result is compared to verify consistency. Hardware lockstep means that\nthe hardware has specific equipment to make this double-/multi-execution transparent.\nSoftware lockstep is another technique that allows providing a similar property without\nrequiring the use of dedicated hardware.\nDepending on the Safety Level, as well as the Safety Concept employed, software lock-\nstep may involve executing multiple times the same software, in parallel or sequentially,\nbut may also involve running multiple separate implementations of the same algorithm.\n7.6.1.3 Full Determinism\nFor Full Determinism, each time a calculation is started, its results are available before\na specified deadline and only depend on the input data, i.e. both Time and Data\nDeterminism must be guaranteed.\nNon-deterministic behavior may arise from different reasons; for example insufficient\ncomputing resources, or uncoordinated access of data, potentially by multiple threads\n77 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P78_155",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 78,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nrunning on multiple processor cores. The order in which the threads access such data\nwill affect the result, which makes it non-deterministic (race condition).\nA fully deterministic calculation must be designed, implemented and integrated in a\nway such that it is independent of processor load caused by other functions and cal-\nculations, sporadic unrelated events, race conditions, deviating random numbers etc.,\ni.e. for the same input and initial conditions it always produces the same result within\na given time.\n7.6.2 Deterministic Client\nAs explained in 7.6.1, future systems need high computing performance in combina-\ntion with high ASIL safety goals. In this chapter we specify mechanisms which support\ndeterministic multithread execution to support high performance software lockstep so-\nlutions. Here are some additional rationales behind it:\n•\nSafety goals for Highly Automated Driving (HAD) systems can be up to ASIL D.\n•\nHigh Performance Computing (HPC) demands can only be met by non\nautomotive-grade, e.g. consumer electronics (CE), microprocessors, which have\nhigh transient hardware error rates compared to automotive-grade microcon-\ntrollers. Most likely no such microprocessor is available for ASIL above B, at\nleast for the parts relevant to the design.\n•\nTo deal with high error rates, ASIL C/D HAD applications require specific mea-\nsures, in particular software lockstep, where execution is done redundantly\nthrough two different paths and the result is compared to detect errors.\n•\nTo make these redundant calculations comparable, software lockstep requires a\nfully deterministic calculation as defined in 7.6.1.3.\n•\nTo meet HPC demands, highly predictable and reliable multi-threading must be\nsupported\nTwo redundant\nprocesses\n, which run in an internal cycle, get in each cycle the same\ninput data via regular interfaces of\nCommunication Management\nand produce (in\nthe absence of errors) the same results, due to full deterministic execution.\nExecution Management\nprovides\nDeterministicClient\nAPIs to support control\nof the process-internal cycle, a deterministic worker pool, activation time stamps and\nrandom numbers. In case of multiple\nprocesses\nfor redundant execution, the\nDeter-\nministicClient\ninteracts with a\nDeterministicSyncMaster\nto ensure identical\nbehavior of the redundantly executed\nprocesses\n.\nThe activation time stamps are provided by local time sychronization slave or mas-\nter, and the redundant executions between the\nprocesses\nare handled by the corre-\nsponding\nDeterministicSyncMaster\n, which propagates the activation time stamp\n78 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P79_156",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 79,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nand the calculated cycle information for next execution to all the connected\nDeter-\nministicClient\n. The calculated data of the application\nprocesses\nis published\nthrough\nCommunication Management\n.\nFor each execution cycle, the\nDeterministicSyncMaster\nsynchronizes the\nDe-\nterministicClient\ns. It makes sure that random numbers and activation time\nstamps that are sent to\nDeterministicClient\ns are identical for the redundantly ex-\necution. The\nDeterministicClient\ns then synchronize the triggering of execution\nbased on the received activation time stamps. An optional software lockstep framework\nmay subscribe to the output of the redundant\nprocesses\nand compare the output to\ndetect failures (e.g. transient processor core or memory errors due to radiation) in\none of the redundant\nprocesses\n. This infrastructure layer can span over multiple\nhardware instances and is implementation specific.\nThe\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nneeds to provide some library functions to sup-\nport redundant deterministic execution with sufficient isolation. The library functions\n(\nDeterministicClient\n) run in the context of the user\nprocess\n. Figure 7.16 con-\nsiders how\nDeterministicClient\ncan be used in one of the redundantly executed\nprocesses\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P79_157",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 79,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.16: Cyclic Deterministic Execution\nCyclic\nprocess\nbehavior is controlled by a wait point API. The API returns a code\nto control the process mode (register services/ service discovery/ init/ run/ termi-\nnate). The execution is triggered by the\nara::exec::DeterministicClient\n(see\n79 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P80_158",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_02210",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 80,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_EM_02210]), depending on a defined period or on received events. Within a\nprocess\n, all input data is available via ara::com (polling-based access only) when\nexecution starts and is stable over one execution cycle. For details see 7.6.3.1.\nThe workload can be deployed to a worker pool API, which allows deterministic execu-\ntion of a set of container elements (e.g. data sets), which are processed in parallel by\nthe same runnable object (i.e. application function). The runnable object is not allowed\nto exchange any information while it is running, i.e. it doesn't access data which can be\naltered by other instances of the runnable object to avoid race conditions. The runnable\nobject instances can physically run in parallel or sequentially in any order. For details\nsee 7.6.3.2.\nAdditional\nDeterministicClient\nAPIs provide random numbers and activation time\nstamps. Common HAD algorithms use particle filters which require random numbers.\nIf used from within the worker pool, the random numbers are assigned to specific con-\ntainer elements to allow deterministic redundant execution. The activation time stamps\ndon't change until the\nprocess\nreaches its next wait point. For deterministic redun-\ndant execution, random number seeds and time stamps need to be synchronized. For\ndetails see 7.6.3.3 and 7.6.3.4.\nAt the end of the execution cycle, the\nprocess\nreturns to the wait point and waits for\nthe next activation.\nThe APIs of\nDeterministicClient\nare standardized and provide abstraction of the\napplication deployment on the actual hardware. The implementation is vendor specific\nand needs to be configured at integration time individually for each\nprocess\nwhich\nuses it.\nThe\nDeterministicClient\nClass is only local to the\nprocess\n. Therefore, there is\ncurrently no security concern foreseen for this API.\nDifferent variants of the\nDeterministicClient\nmight work in a software lockstep\nenvironment or stand-alone, to support cyclic execution and deterministic worker pools.\n[SWS_EM_02551]\n{OBSOLETE}\nMissing DeterministicClient\n⌈\nIf the configuration of\nDeterministicClient\nis missing then\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::\nWaitForActivation\nshall return Error\nkFailed\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00053)\n80 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.17: Deterministic Execution Interface\n7.6.3 Cyclic Deterministic Execution\nThis section describes the APIs shown in Figure 7.16, and how they need to be used\nby a\nprocess\nto execute deterministically, so the\nprocess\ncan be transparently inte-\ngrated into a software lockstep environment.\n7.6.3.1 Control of Cyclic Execution\nExecution Management\nprovides an API to trigger and control recurring, i.e. cyclic\nexecution of the main thread code within a\nprocess\n.\n[SWS_EM_01301]\n{OBSOLETE}\nCyclic Execution\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall\nprovide a blocking wait point API\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::Wait-\nForActivation\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00052, RS_EM_00113)\nAfter the\nprocess\nhas been started by\nExecution Management\n, it reports\nara::\nexec::ExecutionState kRunning\n(see 7.4.1) and calls\nara::exec::Deter-\nministicClient::WaitForActivation\n.\n81 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P82_161",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01302",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 82,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe\nprocess\nexecutes one cycle when\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::\nWaitForActivation\nreturns and then calls the API again to wait for the next activa-\ntion.\nA return value controls the internal lifecycle (e.g. init, run, terminate) of the\nprocess\n,\nsee Figure 7.16. The return codes are used to synchronize the behavior of two\npro-\ncesses\nin case they are executed redundantly.\n[SWS_EM_01302]\n{OBSOLETE}\nCyclic Execution Control\n⌈\nara::exec::Deter-\nministicClient::WaitForActivation\nshall return a code to control the execu-\ntion mode of the calling\nprocess\n. Possible codes are\nkRegisterServices\n,\nkSer-\nviceDiscovery\n,\nkInit\n,\nkRun\n, and\nkTerminate\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00052)\nThe\nara::exec::ActivationReturnType\n(see [SWS_EM_02201]) returned from\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::WaitForActivation\ndetermines the ac-\ntions taken at each cycle:\n•\nkRegisterServices\n The\nprocess\nregisters its communication services, i.e.\nthe services it offers via\nCommunication Management\n. This should be the\nonly occasion for performing service registering. No other functionality should be\nperformed in this step to limit resource consumption and runtime, so no dedicated\nbudget needs to be assigned.\n•\nkServiceDiscovery\n The\nprocess\ndoes communication service discovery.\nThis should be the only occasion for performing service discovery, except a ser-\nvice needs to be replaced later (see ([SWS_EM_01304]). No other functionality\nshould be performed in this step to limit resource consumption and runtime, so\nno dedicated budget needs to be assigned.\n•\nkInit\n The\nprocess\ninitializes its internal data structures. The worker pool\n(see 7.6.3.2) can be accessed once or several time sequentially. A budget (see\n7.6.3.5) needs to be assigned to the Init cycle.\n•\nkRun\n The\nprocess\nperforms one cycle of its normal cyclic execution. This can\nbe repeated indefinitely. The worker pool (see 7.6.3.2) can be accessed once\nor several times sequentially within a cycle. A budget (see 7.6.3.5) needs to be\nassigned.\n•\nkTerminate\n The deterministic client prepares to terminate. It is up to the\nprocess\nwhether this also leads to the actual termination of the\nprocess\nand\nif so the actual termination is performed according to [SWS_EM_01404], see\nSection 7.4.2.\n[SWS_EM_01303]\n{OBSOLETE}\nCyclic Execution Control Sequence\n⌈\nThe return\ncode of\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::WaitForActivation\nshall follow\nthis sequence:\nkRegisterServices\n,\nkServiceDiscovery\n,\nkInit\n,\nkRun\n, and\nkTerminate\n. Note that\nkRun\nis expected to be returned multiple times.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_-\n00052)\n[SWS_EM_01304]\n{OBSOLETE}\nService Modification\n⌈\nIn case a service which is ac-\ncessed by the\nprocess\nneeds to be replaced (e.g. due to unavailability) while the\n82 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P83_162",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01351",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 83,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nkRun\ncycles are executed,\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::WaitForAc-\ntivation\nshall return\nkServiceDiscovery\nonce immediately after\nara::exec::\nDeterministicClient::WaitForActivation\nis called, and then continue with\nthe normal\nkRun\ncycle.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00051, RS_EM_00052)\nThe service discovery update needs to be triggered in an implementation specific way,\ne.g. through a callback triggered by\nStartFindService\nindicating service unavail-\nability. Because the service discovery update runs in addition to the\nkRun\nexecution\nwithin a\nkRun\ncycle, the worst case execution time estimation and budget assignment\nneed to consider that\nkRun\nand\nkServiceDiscovery\nmight run sequentially within\nthe configured execution cycle time (see below).\nThe point in time when\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::WaitForActiva-\ntion\nreturns with\nkRegisterServices\n,\nkServiceDiscovery\n,\nkInit\n,\nkRun\n(first\nkRun\ncycle only, otherwise see below) or\nkTerminate\nis implementation specific. In\ncase of redundant execution, the sequences need to be synchronized.\nThe activation behavior of the\nkRun\n-cycles can be realized by\nExecution Manage-\nment\ntogether with the\nCommunication Management\nas required by the safety con-\ncept. Execution can be triggered via two distinct mechanisms.\n•\nPeriodic activation means that\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::\nWaitForActivation\nreturns periodically based on a configured period.\n•\nEvent-triggered activation means that\nara::exec::Deterministic-\nClient::WaitForActivation\nreturns based on the communication-\nevent-triggers that are configured for the\nprocess\nfrom the outside via\nCommunication Management\n, e.g. by external units, events generated due to\nthe arrival of data or timer events.\nDetails of the synchronization for both periodic and event-triggered activation are dis-\ncussed in section 7.6.4.\n[SWS_EM_01351]\n{OBSOLETE}\nExecution Cycle Time\n⌈\nara::exec::Determin-\nisticClient::WaitForActivation\nshall return\nkRun\nwhen a configurable\ncy-\ncleTimeValue\n(as measured from the last return of\nkRun\n) has been reached.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nEM_00052)\n[SWS_EM_02550]\n{OBSOLETE}\nExecution Cycle Termination\n⌈\nara::exec::\nDeterministicClient::WaitForActivation\nshall return\nkTerminate\nwhen\nthe\nkRun\n-cycle is to be terminated by either exceeding the\nkRun\nloop count\n[SWS_EM_01323] or by\nDeterministicSyncMaster\nsynchronization response\n[SWS_EM_01326].\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00052)\n[SWS_EM_01352]\n{OBSOLETE}\nExecution Cycle Timeout\n⌈\nara::exec::Deter-\nministicClient::WaitForActivation\nshall return error\nkCycleOverrun\nif the\nprevious cycle did overrun (i.e. configured\ncycleTimeValue\nhas been exceeded).\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00052)\n83 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P84_163",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01352",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 84,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nNote that with respect to [SWS_EM_01352], the deterministic client used by the Ap-\nplication detects the\ncycleTimeValue\noverrun and reports it to the application. The\nApplication developer/System Designer can then take the relevant project-specific ac-\ntions.\n[SWS_EM_01353]\n{OBSOLETE}\nEvent-triggered Cycle Activation\n⌈\nIf the configured\ncycleTimeValue\nis zero,\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::WaitForAc-\ntivation\nshall support event triggered activation.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00052)\nDeterministicSyncMaster\nprovides support for event triggered\nara::\nexec::DeterministicClient::WaitForActivation\n(see Section 7.6.4.1)\nas well as synchronized cyclic execution. In these cases the return from\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::WaitForActivation\nis synchronized\nthrough a\nSynchronization Response Message\nfrom\nDeterministicSyncMaster\n[SWS_EM_01326][SWS_EM_01327][SWS_EM_01327].\nThis cyclic behavior can be used in a software lockstep environment to initialize and\ntrigger execution of redundant\nprocesses\nand compare the results after a cycle has\nfinished. For redundant execution, the execution behavior and its budget (activation\ntiming, computing time, computing resources) should be explicitly visible at integration\ntime to configure\nExecution Management\naccordingly.\nOptionally, e.g. if necessary for a software lockstep implementation, all input data as\nreceived via\nCommunication Management\nshould be available when a cycle starts\nand guaranteed to be deterministically consistent.\n7.6.3.2 Worker Pool\n[SWS_EM_01305]\n{OBSOLETE}\nWorker Pool\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall pro-\nvide a blocking API\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::RunWorkerPool\nto\nrun a deterministic worker pool to be used within the\nprocess\nexecution cycle.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nEM_00053)\nThe worker pool is triggered by the main-thread of the\nprocess\nin a sequential order.\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::RunWorkerPool\nis blocking and therefore\nthere is no parallelism between the main-thread and the worker pool. The user\npro-\ncess\nis not allowed to create threads on its own by using normal POSIX mechanisms\nto avoid the risk of inducing indeterministic behavior.\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::RunWorkerPool\nregisters a\nrunnableObj\n, along with a\ncontainer\n. The\ncontainer\ncontains a set of\nobjects, which are processed in parallel by the the\ncontainer\ninvoked from multiple\nworkers (e.g. based on POSIX threads) in the pool (see Figure 7.18). This means, the\ndeterministic worker pool is used to process a set of\ncontainer\nelements, which are\nthe parameters to the\nrunnableObj\n. Each element in the\ncontainer\nrepresents a\njob to be computed. The deterministic distribution of the elements to individual workers\nis done by using the container iterator.\n84 of 197 Document ID 721: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P85_164",
      "source_element": "SWS_EM_01306",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement",
      "source_page": 85,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_EM_01306]\n{OBSOLETE}\nprocessing Container Objects\n⌈\nara::exec::De-\nterministicClient::RunWorkerPool\nshall sequentially (using the iterator of in-\nput parameter\ncontainer\n) call a method\nara::exec::WorkerRunnable::Run\n(input parameter\nrunnableObj\n) on every element of\ncontainer\n, by using a worker\npool of size\nnumberOfWorkers\n.\n⌋\n(RS_EM_00053)\nThe Worker object passed to\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::RunWork-\nerPool\nis an instance of\nara::exec::WorkerRunnable\n. This would typically be\nachieved through a sub-class derived from\nara::exec::WorkerRunnable\nusing\npublic inheritance to enable project-specification extensions to be added.\nWithin\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::RunWorkerPool\nthe elements of\ncontainer\nare iteratively processed by the background worker pool. If more ele-\nments are available than workers then sequential processing will occur. In pseudo-\ncode (ignoring parallelisation) the method\nara::exec::DeterministicClient::\nRunWorkerPool\nbehaves as follows:"

      "id": "SNIP_exec_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_E_P86_165",
      "source_element": null,
